{"body":"## Purpose
Define append-only result/event rows so worker decisions, outputs, failures, and agent answers are not lost in terminal scrollback.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Makes `worker -> events.jsonl` the durable observation boundary. |
| product | Allows every adapter to report the same event vocabulary. |
| system/org | Enables non-TUI operation with later readback. |
| business/meta | Turns runs into evidence assets, not ephemeral actions. |

## Scope
- Define row kinds: `accepted`, `started`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `completed`, `failed`, `blocked`.
- Define link fields to instruction id and run id.
- Define minimal final-answer and error fields.

## Non-scope
- Session list projection.
- UI rendering.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `spec/result/v1.md` or equivalent exists.
- [ ] One execution can be reconstructed from result rows alone.
- [ ] Adapter outputs map into the same result vocabulary.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Agent final answer exists only in stdout scrollback.
- [ ] Failure reason is not represented as JSONL.

## Evidence
- Contract doc.
- Fixture run with success and failure events.

## Merge condition
Merge only when a reviewer can reconstruct what happened without opening a TUI."}

request.text:
{"body":"## 背景

UIには再利用するライブラリと、それを利用するshell・OPSがある。仕様、意味処理、描画、部品の接続を同じものとして説明すると、利用先ごとに処理や状態の所有者が分かれやすい。

本Issueは#207の完成物を基点に、責務と依存を少数の一貫した言葉で説明できる状態を目指す。#207の範囲・完了条件は変更しない。shellの独立公開と4利用面の完成状態は roccho-dev/adrs#382 を参照し、本Issueへ重複記載しない。

## ゴール状態

```text
UI Library
├─ protocols
├─ cores
└─ adapters

Consumers
├─ shell
└─ ops
```

| 分類 | 責務 |
|---|---|
| protocols | データ・メッセージ・操作の契約 |
| cores | 利用先や描画環境に依存しない意味・状態・処理 |
| adapters | core / protocolと具体的な描画・実行環境との接続 |
| consumers | 公開契約から必要な部品を選択・接続して利用する側 |

shellとOPSは、ライブラリを利用する立場では同格である。これは同じ責務・同じAPIをすべて持つという意味ではない。shellはUI repo内、OPSは外部repoという配置の違いも維持できる。host / compositionは部品を接続・起動する責務の呼び方であり、ライブラリを統括する別の意味処理層にはしない。

A2UIの仕様・メッセージはprotocol、A2UIをブラウザへ接続・表示する実装はadapterとして区別する。

semantic-mapのdomain / projectionは描画環境に依存しない処理として説明し、SemanticMapEditorCoreはsemantic-mapの操作・編集を統括する。UI全体を統括する万能Coreとせず、無関係なcodecやA2UIの処理を集めない。semantic-map内部の正式な操作経路・状態の所有は#207に従う。

## 結論

同じUI能力について、shell用とOPS用に意味処理・codec・projection・描画処理の正本を複製しない。consumer固有の接続・起動処理と、共通ライブラリの責務を区別する。

成功は物理ディレクトリ名を揃えることではなく、実装上の責務・依存・所有者がこの分類で一意に説明できることである。既存構成で満たせるならコード変更は不要とし、見た目を揃えるためだけの移動、新package、万能Core、新frameworkは作らない。"}

request.text:
{"body":"## 背景

UIには再利用するライブラリと、それを利用するshell・OPSがある。仕様、意味処理、描画、部品の接続を同じものとして説明すると、利用先ごとに処理や状態の所有者が分かれやすい。

本Issueは#207の完成物を基点に、責務と依存を少数の一貫した言葉で説明できる状態を目指す。#207の範囲・完了条件は変更しない。shellの独立公開と4利用面の完成状態は roccho-dev/adrs#382 を参照し、本Issueへ重複記載しない。

## ゴール状態

```text
UI Library
├─ protocols
├─ cores
└─ adapters

Consumers
├─ shell
└─ ops
```

| 分類 | 責務 |
|---|---|
| protocols | データ・メッセージ・操作の契約 |
| cores | 利用先や描画環境に依存しない意味・状態・処理 |
| adapters | core / protocolと具体的な描画・実行環境との接続 |
| consumers | 公開契約から必要な部品を選択・接続して利用する側 |

shellとOPSは、ライブラリを利用する立場では同格である。これは同じ責務・同じAPIをすべて持つという意味ではない。shellはUI repo内、OPSは外部repoという配置の違いも維持できる。host / compositionは部品を接続・起動する責務の呼び方であり、ライブラリを統括する別の意味処理層にはしない。

A2UIの仕様・メッセージはprotocol、A2UIをブラウザへ接続・表示する実装はadapterとして区別する。

semantic-mapのdomain / projectionは描画環境に依存しない処理として説明し、SemanticMapEditorCoreはsemantic-mapの操作・編集を統括する。UI全体を統括する万能Coreとせず、無関係なcodecやA2UIの処理を集めない。semantic-map内部の正式な操作経路・状態の所有は#207に従う。

## 結論

同じUI能力について、shell用とOPS用に意味処理・codec・projection・描画処理の正本を複製しない。consumer固有の接続・起動処理と、共通ライブラリの責務を区別する。

成功は物理ディレクトリ名を揃えることではなく、実装上の責務・依存・所有者がこの分類で一意に説明できることである。既存構成で満たせるならコード変更は不要とし、見た目を揃えるためだけの移動、新package、万能Core、新frameworkは作らない。"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Prove the full local/dev path: UI target selection, Vim/hq command confirmation, queue append, worker processing, projection update, UI update, and receipt.

## Completion state

This is complete when one proof command reproduces the whole path without treating queue, UI, projection, or generated artifacts as authority.

## Proof flow

1. Select a node or edge in localhost UI.
2. Export `ui.targetRef.v1` to `.local/current-target.json`.
3. Vim/hq reads the targetRef.
4. `model.*` command is completed and confirmed.
5. `.local/queue.jsonl` receives `hq.modelCommitQueued.v1`.
6. Local worker reads queue.
7. Shadow model updates.
8. Projection regenerates.
9. Localhost UI hot reloads.
10. `.local/receipt.jsonl` receives `hq.receipt.v1`.
11. Proof report returns PASS.

## Scope

- One proof command.
- Before/after projection digests.
- Queue append proof.
- Projection update proof.
- UI visible update proof.
- Receipt proof.
- Non-authority proof.

## Done checklist

- [ ] One command runs the proof.
- [ ] Before projection digest is recorded.
- [ ] After projection digest is recorded.
- [ ] Digest changes after valid command.
- [ ] UI visible state changes.
- [ ] Receipt includes queue id.
- [ ] Receipt includes targetRef.
- [ ] Receipt includes projection digest.
- [ ] Proof says queue is not authority.
- [ ] Proof works without accepted ledger for local/dev.
- [ ] Proof can later be extended to admission/ledger path.

## Non-scope

- Production admission completion.
- Multi-user queue.
- Remote GitHub issue-comment persistence.
- Full source archive extraction."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Add destructive provenance fixtures so gov-package-output producer and verifier work cannot pass only on happy-path packet generation.

Parent phase issue: #79

## Scope

This is an issue for a future governance implementation PR. Do not open or implement the PR from this issue alone.

## Requirements

- Add clean fixture for a valid gov-produced packet.
- Add shape-only packet fixture with no producer provenance.
- Add fake matching provenance fixture.
- Add stale `producerRev` fixture.
- Add wrong `producerDigest` fixture.
- Add missing input path fixture.
- Add wrong `inputLockDigest` fixture.
- Add wrong `outputDigest` fixture.
- Add undeclared source input fixture if supported by the producer design.
- Add non-deterministic output fixture or equivalent deterministic check.
- Assert that destructive fixtures fail with stable diagnostic classes.
- Assert that destructive fixture findings include expected/actual/delta/likelyOwner/nextAction.
- Ensure fixture names do not imply production enforcement or branch protection.

## Done when

- A future PR adds destructive provenance fixtures alongside the clean fixture.
- Each destructive fixture fails for the intended reason.
- Failure diagnostics are stable and actionable.
- Fixtures cover B1/B2/C2/C3 escape hatches.
- Fixture CI is tool/provenance quality evidence, not final merge authority.

## Not done when

- Only happy-path packet generation is tested.
- Fake provenance can pass.
- Missing source input can pass.
- Wrong output digest can pass.
- Destructive fixtures fail for vague or unstable reasons.
- PR claims final gate, branch protection, or downstream rollout.

## Evidence required in child PR

- Clean fixture path.
- Destructive fixture paths.
- Check command or CI surface that runs them.
- Expected diagnostic class matrix.
- Example failure output containing expected/actual/delta/nextAction.

## Child PR comment template

```text
Child PR: governance#<number>
Phase issue: #79 / C4
Requirement: destructive gov-package-output provenance fixtures
Delta removed: producer/verifier can no longer prove only the happy path
Evidence: <fixture paths / diagnostic matrix / checks>
Boundary: fixture/selftest only; no final gate/cutover/branch protection claim
```
"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Add destructive provenance fixtures so gov-package-output producer and verifier work cannot pass only on happy-path packet generation.

Parent phase issue: #79

## Scope

This is an issue for a future governance implementation PR. Do not open or implement the PR from this issue alone.

## Requirements

- Add clean fixture for a valid gov-produced packet.
- Add shape-only packet fixture with no producer provenance.
- Add fake matching provenance fixture.
- Add stale `producerRev` fixture.
- Add wrong `producerDigest` fixture.
- Add missing input path fixture.
- Add wrong `inputLockDigest` fixture.
- Add wrong `outputDigest` fixture.
- Add undeclared source input fixture if supported by the producer design.
- Add non-deterministic output fixture or equivalent deterministic check.
- Assert that destructive fixtures fail with stable diagnostic classes.
- Assert that destructive fixture findings include expected/actual/delta/likelyOwner/nextAction.
- Ensure fixture names do not imply production enforcement or branch protection.

## Done when

- A future PR adds destructive provenance fixtures alongside the clean fixture.
- Each destructive fixture fails for the intended reason.
- Failure diagnostics are stable and actionable.
- Fixtures cover B1/B2/C2/C3 escape hatches.
- Fixture CI is tool/provenance quality evidence, not final merge authority.

## Not done when

- Only happy-path packet generation is tested.
- Fake provenance can pass.
- Missing source input can pass.
- Wrong output digest can pass.
- Destructive fixtures fail for vague or unstable reasons.
- PR claims final gate, branch protection, or downstream rollout.

## Evidence required in child PR

- Clean fixture path.
- Destructive fixture paths.
- Check command or CI surface that runs them.
- Expected diagnostic class matrix.
- Example failure output containing expected/actual/delta/nextAction.

## Child PR comment template

```text
Child PR: governance#<number>
Phase issue: #79 / C4
Requirement: destructive gov-package-output provenance fixtures
Delta removed: producer/verifier can no longer prove only the happy path
Evidence: <fixture paths / diagnostic matrix / checks>
Boundary: fixture/selftest only; no final gate/cutover/branch protection claim
```
"}

{"body":"## 背景

多数のagentを同時に動かすと、個別のissue / PR / worktree / logを読むUIだけでは「組織全体が今どう動いているか」を把握できない。

欲しいのは、遠目では詳細を読まずに次だけ分かる Control UI です。

- 進んでいるか
- どこで作業しているか
- 何を見て作業しているか
- scope目的 / meta目的 / 組織規約 / コード規約へ目線が通っているか
- どこが止まっているか
- 同一scope内で何本の作業が並行しているか

詳細は常時表示しない。必要なときだけ click / zoom / focus で issue / PR / worktree / evidence / log まで降りる。

これは「巨大な組織図」を作る話ではなく、**N次元の実行状態を2Dへ薄くprojectionし、遠景では組織の生体反応だけを読む**ためのUIです。

## 現状との関係

### Control UI

現在の Control UI は `rel.parent` を使う単一root TreeGridで、scope → child の再帰表示と relation-kind 単位のcollapseを持つ。

- `packages/control/src/control-graph.mjs`
- `packages/a2ui-browser/src/catalog/control.mjs`
- `examples/control/**`

これは「scope配下の構成員・項目」を読むには小さく強い。一方、同一scopeで複数agent / worktree / issueが同時進行する **parallel activity の遠景把握**には弱い。

### Purpose Atlas / AtlasStage

Purpose Atlas は今回の方向に近い。

- purpose / responsibility / focus のlens
- selection → Inspector
- purpose → gap → work order → receipt → residual
- A2UIをstate/action契約として使い、重い描画をportへ逃がす
- AtlasStageはsafe SVG DOMを直接生成する
- ui.gitはstate authorityを持たない

関連:
- #161 AtlasStage SVG port
- #108 Contract Model Atlas read-model
- #111 repo map semantic LOD
- #114 camera adapter
- #116 context-preserving LOD

ただし既存のrepo-map LODはrepo/package/modelの地図が対象であり、このIssueが扱う **agent organization / live activity / live reference / parallel work** は別責務。

## 最上位目的

高価値法人を、少ない人間監視コストで多数agentにより運営できる状態を作る。

このUIの価値は「見栄え」ではなく、**人間が多数agentの全体状態を数秒で判断できること**。

---

## 期待要件

| # | 期待 | 背景 |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 多数のagent組織を一目で見る | 個別ログではなく全体の生存状態を読む |
| 2 | 遠景でも活動が分かる | node / edge の光・流れで「進んでいる」を認識する |
| 3 | 何を見て作業しているか分かる | scope目的、meta目的、組織規約、コード規約への参照を読む |
| 4 | 詳細は常時不要 | issue / PR / worktree / evidence / log はclick/zoom後でよい |
| 5 | 全体把握のためのzoom-outを要求しない | 全体を見るために文字を極小化しない |
| 6 | semantic zoom | 遠景 / 中景 / 近景で見せる意味そのものを変える |
| 7 | Project / scope が基本単位 | scope配下に作業・構成員を置く現在のControl形と整合する |
| 8 | Projectにも階層がある | Portfolio → Product → Project → Workstream を再帰的に扱う |
| 9 | Project階層はnested area | scopeを空間の包含として遠目で読む |
| 10 | 組織にも独立した階層がある | CEO → CTO → Lead → Agent はProject階層とは別 |
| 11 | 組織関係をProjectへ従属させない | CTO–COOなどscopeを跨ぐ関係を失わない |
| 12 | 組織階層はnode + edge | Project areaとは別visual channelへ割り当てる |
| 13 | Agent nodeを重複表示しない | 組織用/Project用に同じagentを複製しない |
| 14 | 並行開発を強く見る | 同一scopeで複数worktree/issue/agentが同時進行することが難所 |
| 15 | 並行性をlane / density / activity位置で読む | 遠景では「何本走っているか」を優先する |
| 16 | 意味の次元はN次元でよい | 画面自体をN次元化しない |
| 17 | 意味次元を別visual channelへ割り当てる | XYにすべて押し込まない |
| 18 | 常時見せる次元を絞る | 遠景は3〜5次元程度、残りはinteractionへ逃がす |
| 19 | 状態=色、活動=光/motion | visual channelの責務を重複させない |
| 20 | 依存・参照=edge | 所属より「何を見て今動いたか」を追えることを重視 |
| 21 | HTML > SVG > HTML を許す | outer HTML=SSE/UI、SVG=空間/edge/camera、foreignObject HTML=node detail |
| 22 | SSEで現状を投影可能 | UI自身をstate storeにしない |
| 23 | sampleはHTML単体で即見える | 外部data/SSEなしでもprojectionを確認可能にする |
| 24 | Controlを遠景で読めるUIへ拡張可能 | 現TreeGridは詳細一覧に強いが組織の生体反応には弱い |
| 25 | UIは意味を所有しすぎない | 同じN次元stateから別projectionを作れるようにする |

## 意味次元 → visual channel

この割当はsource dataのschemaではなく、projection ruleとして扱う。

| 意味 | 遠景表現 |
|---|---|
| Project / scope hierarchy | nested area |
| Organization hierarchy | node position + org edge |
| dependency / reference | edge |
| state | color |
| live activity | light / pulse / flowing edge |
| parallel work | lane / density / multiple activity points |
| importance | size / intensity（必要時のみ） |
| detail | semantic zoom / click / focus |

原則:

> Project hierarchy = 空間の包含  
> Organization hierarchy = 独立graph  
> Agent = 1 node  
> Work/reference = edge/activity  
> Detail = interactionで後出し

Project areaの中へ組織graphを閉じ込めてはいけない。組織edgeはscopeを横断できる。

## 遠景 / 中景 / 近景

```text
far:
  Project / scope areas
  live activity
  reference path
  blocked / abnormal
  parallel density

middle:
  agent
  parallel lane / worktree
  local dependency
  active purpose / policy references

near:
  issue
  PR
  worktree
  exact rule
  evidence
  log / receipt
```

zoomは単なるgeometry scaleではなく、**semantic LODの入力**として使う。

## 最小アーキテクチャ

```text
N-dimensional external state
          |
          v
projection / LOD reducer
          |
          v
HTML
└─ SVG
   ├─ nested areas      Project hierarchy
   ├─ org edges         Organization hierarchy
   ├─ work/ref edges    dependency / reference
   ├─ light / motion    live activity
   └─ foreignObject
      └─ HTML node      detail on demand
```

### authority boundary

```text
external state / events
       |
       | SSE / attached data / projection input
       v
ui projection
       |
       +--> pixels
       +--> interaction proposal
```

- ui.gitはaccepted business stateを所有しない
- live activityを永続authorityにしない
- camera / selection / hoverはlocal transient stateでよい
- rendererはsource modelの意味を再定義しない

## 既存資産との境界

### 再利用候補

- AtlasStageのsafe SVG primitive
- Purpose Atlasのfocus / selection / inspector概念
- #111/#114/#116 のsemantic LOD / context preservation / camera分離
- Controlのrel.parent / relation-kind / collapseという詳細projection
- A2UIのstate/action/port boundary

### このIssueで新しく閉じるもの

- agent organizationを遠景で読むprojection
- live activity visual channel
- live reference visual channel
- parallel work visual channel
- Project hierarchy + Organization hierarchy の同時projection
- semantic LODで far→middle→near を切り替える規則

## 重要な設計判断

1. **別々の「組織図」と「Project図」を作らない。**
   - 同じAgent nodeを重複させない。

2. **Project hierarchy と Organization hierarchy を同じparentに押し込まない。**
   - Project = nested area
   - Org = graph

3. **遠景で詳細文字を読ませない。**
   - activity / reference / abnormalityを先に読む。

4. **zoomだけで解決しない。**
   - semantic LODで情報密度を変える。

5. **全edgeを常時表示しない。**
   - focus / activity / abnormalityに必要なedgeだけprojectionする。

6. **rendererに意味を埋め込みすぎない。**
   - visual channel割当はprojection側の責務。

## 完成条件

以下を1つのstandalone HTML proofで確認できれば、最小sliceは閉じる。

- [ ] 2階層以上のProject nested areaが見える
- [ ] Projectを跨ぐOrganization edgeが見える
- [ ] 同じAgentが1 nodeとしてのみ存在する
- [ ] 1 Project内で3本以上のparallel workが遠景から認識できる
- [ ] active node / edgeが静止画でも判別でき、motion有効時は活動として認識できる
- [ ] agent → scope/meta purpose または policy/code rule のreference pathが遠景で分かる
- [ ] blocked / stoppedがactiveと区別できる
- [ ] farではdetail textを隠しても意味が残る
- [ ] zoom-inでagent/work、さらに近景でissue/PR/worktree/evidenceへsemantic LODする
- [ ] clickでnode detailを出せる
- [ ] fitで全体へ戻れる
- [ ] source stateとprojection/camera stateが分離されている
- [ ] external live inputを差し替えてもrenderer自体の意味契約を変えない

## 非スコープ

- 3D / WebGL化
- VR的な空間次元追加
- 新しいstate store
- ui.gitをruntime authorityにすること
- 全種類のagent eventを最初から可視化すること
- 全edgeを常時描くこと
- Control TreeGridの即時廃止
- Purpose Atlasの即時置換
- repo-map LOD実装の再実装

## 最重要UX原則

> **遠目では「どこが動き、何を見ているか」だけ分かる。**  
> **近づいた時だけ「誰が、何を、なぜ」を読む。**

"}

{"body":"## 背景

多数のagentを同時に動かすと、個別のissue / PR / worktree / logを読むUIだけでは「組織全体が今どう動いているか」を把握できない。

欲しいのは、遠目では詳細を読まずに次だけ分かる Control UI です。

- 進んでいるか
- どこで作業しているか
- 何を見て作業しているか
- scope目的 / meta目的 / 組織規約 / コード規約へ目線が通っているか
- どこが止まっているか
- 同一scope内で何本の作業が並行しているか

詳細は常時表示しない。必要なときだけ click / zoom / focus で issue / PR / worktree / evidence / log まで降りる。

これは「巨大な組織図」を作る話ではなく、**N次元の実行状態を2Dへ薄くprojectionし、遠景では組織の生体反応だけを読む**ためのUIです。

## 現状との関係

### Control UI

現在の Control UI は `rel.parent` を使う単一root TreeGridで、scope → child の再帰表示と relation-kind 単位のcollapseを持つ。

- `packages/control/src/control-graph.mjs`
- `packages/a2ui-browser/src/catalog/control.mjs`
- `examples/control/**`

これは「scope配下の構成員・項目」を読むには小さく強い。一方、同一scopeで複数agent / worktree / issueが同時進行する **parallel activity の遠景把握**には弱い。

### Purpose Atlas / AtlasStage

Purpose Atlas は今回の方向に近い。

- purpose / responsibility / focus のlens
- selection → Inspector
- purpose → gap → work order → receipt → residual
- A2UIをstate/action契約として使い、重い描画をportへ逃がす
- AtlasStageはsafe SVG DOMを直接生成する
- ui.gitはstate authorityを持たない

関連:
- #161 AtlasStage SVG port
- #108 Contract Model Atlas read-model
- #111 repo map semantic LOD
- #114 camera adapter
- #116 context-preserving LOD

ただし既存のrepo-map LODはrepo/package/modelの地図が対象であり、このIssueが扱う **agent organization / live activity / live reference / parallel work** は別責務。

## 最上位目的

高価値法人を、少ない人間監視コストで多数agentにより運営できる状態を作る。

このUIの価値は「見栄え」ではなく、**人間が多数agentの全体状態を数秒で判断できること**。

---

## 期待要件

| # | 期待 | 背景 |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 多数のagent組織を一目で見る | 個別ログではなく全体の生存状態を読む |
| 2 | 遠景でも活動が分かる | node / edge の光・流れで「進んでいる」を認識する |
| 3 | 何を見て作業しているか分かる | scope目的、meta目的、組織規約、コード規約への参照を読む |
| 4 | 詳細は常時不要 | issue / PR / worktree / evidence / log はclick/zoom後でよい |
| 5 | 全体把握のためのzoom-outを要求しない | 全体を見るために文字を極小化しない |
| 6 | semantic zoom | 遠景 / 中景 / 近景で見せる意味そのものを変える |
| 7 | Project / scope が基本単位 | scope配下に作業・構成員を置く現在のControl形と整合する |
| 8 | Projectにも階層がある | Portfolio → Product → Project → Workstream を再帰的に扱う |
| 9 | Project階層はnested area | scopeを空間の包含として遠目で読む |
| 10 | 組織にも独立した階層がある | CEO → CTO → Lead → Agent はProject階層とは別 |
| 11 | 組織関係をProjectへ従属させない | CTO–COOなどscopeを跨ぐ関係を失わない |
| 12 | 組織階層はnode + edge | Project areaとは別visual channelへ割り当てる |
| 13 | Agent nodeを重複表示しない | 組織用/Project用に同じagentを複製しない |
| 14 | 並行開発を強く見る | 同一scopeで複数worktree/issue/agentが同時進行することが難所 |
| 15 | 並行性をlane / density / activity位置で読む | 遠景では「何本走っているか」を優先する |
| 16 | 意味の次元はN次元でよい | 画面自体をN次元化しない |
| 17 | 意味次元を別visual channelへ割り当てる | XYにすべて押し込まない |
| 18 | 常時見せる次元を絞る | 遠景は3〜5次元程度、残りはinteractionへ逃がす |
| 19 | 状態=色、活動=光/motion | visual channelの責務を重複させない |
| 20 | 依存・参照=edge | 所属より「何を見て今動いたか」を追えることを重視 |
| 21 | HTML > SVG > HTML を許す | outer HTML=SSE/UI、SVG=空間/edge/camera、foreignObject HTML=node detail |
| 22 | SSEで現状を投影可能 | UI自身をstate storeにしない |
| 23 | sampleはHTML単体で即見える | 外部data/SSEなしでもprojectionを確認可能にする |
| 24 | Controlを遠景で読めるUIへ拡張可能 | 現TreeGridは詳細一覧に強いが組織の生体反応には弱い |
| 25 | UIは意味を所有しすぎない | 同じN次元stateから別projectionを作れるようにする |

## 意味次元 → visual channel

この割当はsource dataのschemaではなく、projection ruleとして扱う。

| 意味 | 遠景表現 |
|---|---|
| Project / scope hierarchy | nested area |
| Organization hierarchy | node position + org edge |
| dependency / reference | edge |
| state | color |
| live activity | light / pulse / flowing edge |
| parallel work | lane / density / multiple activity points |
| importance | size / intensity（必要時のみ） |
| detail | semantic zoom / click / focus |

原則:

> Project hierarchy = 空間の包含  
> Organization hierarchy = 独立graph  
> Agent = 1 node  
> Work/reference = edge/activity  
> Detail = interactionで後出し

Project areaの中へ組織graphを閉じ込めてはいけない。組織edgeはscopeを横断できる。

## 遠景 / 中景 / 近景

```text
far:
  Project / scope areas
  live activity
  reference path
  blocked / abnormal
  parallel density

middle:
  agent
  parallel lane / worktree
  local dependency
  active purpose / policy references

near:
  issue
  PR
  worktree
  exact rule
  evidence
  log / receipt
```

zoomは単なるgeometry scaleではなく、**semantic LODの入力**として使う。

## 最小アーキテクチャ

```text
N-dimensional external state
          |
          v
projection / LOD reducer
          |
          v
HTML
└─ SVG
   ├─ nested areas      Project hierarchy
   ├─ org edges         Organization hierarchy
   ├─ work/ref edges    dependency / reference
   ├─ light / motion    live activity
   └─ foreignObject
      └─ HTML node      detail on demand
```

### authority boundary

```text
external state / events
       |
       | SSE / attached data / projection input
       v
ui projection
       |
       +--> pixels
       +--> interaction proposal
```

- ui.gitはaccepted business stateを所有しない
- live activityを永続authorityにしない
- camera / selection / hoverはlocal transient stateでよい
- rendererはsource modelの意味を再定義しない

## 既存資産との境界

### 再利用候補

- AtlasStageのsafe SVG primitive
- Purpose Atlasのfocus / selection / inspector概念
- #111/#114/#116 のsemantic LOD / context preservation / camera分離
- Controlのrel.parent / relation-kind / collapseという詳細projection
- A2UIのstate/action/port boundary

### このIssueで新しく閉じるもの

- agent organizationを遠景で読むprojection
- live activity visual channel
- live reference visual channel
- parallel work visual channel
- Project hierarchy + Organization hierarchy の同時projection
- semantic LODで far→middle→near を切り替える規則

## 重要な設計判断

1. **別々の「組織図」と「Project図」を作らない。**
   - 同じAgent nodeを重複させない。

2. **Project hierarchy と Organization hierarchy を同じparentに押し込まない。**
   - Project = nested area
   - Org = graph

3. **遠景で詳細文字を読ませない。**
   - activity / reference / abnormalityを先に読む。

4. **zoomだけで解決しない。**
   - semantic LODで情報密度を変える。

5. **全edgeを常時表示しない。**
   - focus / activity / abnormalityに必要なedgeだけprojectionする。

6. **rendererに意味を埋め込みすぎない。**
   - visual channel割当はprojection側の責務。

## 完成条件

以下を1つのstandalone HTML proofで確認できれば、最小sliceは閉じる。

- [ ] 2階層以上のProject nested areaが見える
- [ ] Projectを跨ぐOrganization edgeが見える
- [ ] 同じAgentが1 nodeとしてのみ存在する
- [ ] 1 Project内で3本以上のparallel workが遠景から認識できる
- [ ] active node / edgeが静止画でも判別でき、motion有効時は活動として認識できる
- [ ] agent → scope/meta purpose または policy/code rule のreference pathが遠景で分かる
- [ ] blocked / stoppedがactiveと区別できる
- [ ] farではdetail textを隠しても意味が残る
- [ ] zoom-inでagent/work、さらに近景でissue/PR/worktree/evidenceへsemantic LODする
- [ ] clickでnode detailを出せる
- [ ] fitで全体へ戻れる
- [ ] source stateとprojection/camera stateが分離されている
- [ ] external live inputを差し替えてもrenderer自体の意味契約を変えない

## 非スコープ

- 3D / WebGL化
- VR的な空間次元追加
- 新しいstate store
- ui.gitをruntime authorityにすること
- 全種類のagent eventを最初から可視化すること
- 全edgeを常時描くこと
- Control TreeGridの即時廃止
- Purpose Atlasの即時置換
- repo-map LOD実装の再実装

## 最重要UX原則

> **遠目では「どこが動き、何を見ているか」だけ分かる。**  
> **近づいた時だけ「誰が、何を、なぜ」を読む。**

"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Integrate the useful LSP/profile/Vim submit behavior staged in `hq#94` into the canonical hq compiler and acceptance architecture defined by `hq#95`.

This issue owns only the client-to-compiler path:

```text
Vim
  -> vim-lsp
  -> canonical hq LSP transport
  -> completion / diagnostics / explicit human acceptance
  -> accepted.instruction compiler envelope
```

It must not introduce target execution, a second worker lifecycle, or parallel queue/result schemas.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Add the missing LSP transport to the existing canonical compiler contract. |
| Product | Make Vim depend on one official hq artifact and profile contract. |
| Architecture | Keep LSP as an adapter over existing compiler/acceptance semantics. |
| Quality | Prove completion is side-effect free and submit uses canonical acceptance. |
| Operations | Remove dependence on the temporary `ops#83` binary. |
| Transferability | Give every editor client one stable hq LSP surface. |
| meta^10 | Eliminate duplicated compiler behavior and client-specific hidden paths. |

## Depends on

- Parent architecture: `hq#95`
- Migration staging: `hq#94`
- Vim client: `roccho-dev/edits#66`
- Environment plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`

## Scope

### LSP entrypoint

Provide an hq-owned LSP entrypoint equivalent to:

```text
hq lsp --profile <name>
```

The command may be implemented in `cmd/hq` or a dedicated official command if that keeps the compiler boundary smaller. In either case it must reuse the existing compiler/core and acceptance contracts rather than copy them.

### Profile resolution

A profile identifies adapter-provided/generated inputs such as:

- JSONL world/schema/catalog projection
- explicit compiler-intent queue destination or queue port
- contract versions
- environment/deployment identity needed for validation

Profile resolution belongs behind an hq port. The compiler core must not know filesystem layout, GitHub Release URLs, envs registry layout, or Windows installation paths.

### Completion and diagnostics

- `textDocument/didOpen` and `didChange` maintain document text/version.
- `textDocument/completion` delegates to canonical hq completion.
- candidate labels/details/edit intent/compileDraft derive from the same compiler world used by terminal/non-interactive hq.
- completion and diagnostics append zero durable rows and start no process.
- valid Japanese/text and command candidate classes may coexist only through explicit typed candidate metadata; candidate presentation must not create execution meaning.

### Explicit acceptance

Expose one explicit LSP command, provisionally `hq.submit`, that:

1. receives an opaque action generated by the current document version;
2. rejects missing or stale document versions;
3. reuses canonical compiler acceptance/finalization;
4. appends exactly one `accepted.instruction` compiler envelope through the canonical queue port;
5. returns a versioned submit result containing the canonical accepted identity.

The LSP layer must not append `hq.hostCommandQueued.v1` as a parallel durable contract.

### Vim compatibility

The implementation must support the `edits#66` model:

```text
g:hq_bin
  -> hq lsp --profile local
:HqStart
:HqSubmit
```

Vim receives no JSONL path, provider path, worker path, or environment dependency graph.

```

| Generation | Contribution |
|---|---|
| Scope | Add the missing LSP transport to the existing canonical compiler contract. |
| Product | Make Vim depend on one official hq artifact and profile contract. |
| Architecture | Keep LSP as an adapter over existing compiler/acceptance semantics. |
| Quality | Prove completion is side-effect free and submit uses canonical acceptance. |
| Operations | Remove dependence on the temporary `ops#83` binary. |
| Transferability | Give every editor client one stable hq LSP surface. |
| meta^10 | Eliminate duplicated compiler behavior and client-specific hidden paths. |

- Parent architecture: `hq#95`
- Migration staging: `hq#94`
- Vim client: `roccho-dev/edits#66`
- Environment plan: `roccho-dev/envs#4`

Provide an hq-owned LSP entrypoint equivalent to:

```text
hq lsp --profile <name>

- JSONL world/schema/catalog projection

1. receives an opaque action generated by the current document version;
2. rejects missing or stale document versions;
3. reuses canonical compiler acceptance/finalization;
4. appends exactly one `accepted.instruction` compiler envelope through the canonical queue port;
5. returns a versioned submit result containing the canonical accepted identity.

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Separate `hq` into a schema-independent `core+port as lib` and schema-dependent adapters before adding ADRS projected / queue schema adapters.

The intended sequence is strict:

1. First, extract and prove the `core+port as lib` boundary.
2. Then, add adapters for the proposed projected/queue schema.

This prevents ADRS projected schema, queue envelope schema, or target payload schema from leaking into hq core.

Refs #13.

## Final one-line shape

`hq core+port` is a reusable JSONL autocomplete compiler library.

Adapters translate concrete file schemas into and out of that library.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose | Directness |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Separate current behavior from concrete file/schema shapes | Direct |
| 1 | Make `core+port as lib` reusable and schema-independent | Direct |
| 2 | Keep ADRS raw/projected and queue envelope schemas outside core | Direct |
| 3 | Add projected/queue adapters only after the lib boundary is proved | Direct |
| 4 | Preserve file-only operation and append-only queue behavior | Direct |
| 5 | Make UI, hq, ADRS, and future targets reusable through adapters | Direct |
| 6 | Keep the implementation small and easy to sell/maintain | Indirect |
| 7 | Support high-margin software asset creation | Indirect |
| 8 | Support company value and sale-readiness | Meta |

## Non-negotiable dependency rule

| Layer | May depend on concrete schemas? | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| core | No | Owns meaning only |
| port | No | Owns abstract boundaries only |
| adapter | Yes | Owns file/schema translation |
| CLI/REPL runtime | Yes, through adapters | Must not parse concrete schemas inside core |
| tests/fixtures | Yes | Used to prove adapters and protocol behavior |

## Desired dependency direction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Lib["core+port as lib"]
    Core["core: context / suggestion / acceptance / instruction"]
    Port["port: read world / append instruction / clock / id / diagnostics"]
    Core --> Port
  end

  subgraph Adapters["schema adapters"]
    A1["current proof adapter"]
    A2["ADRS projected reader adapter"]
    A3["queue JSONL writer adapter"]
    A4["target payload adapters"]
  end

  subgraph Files["files"]
    F1["adrs.projected.fixed.jsonl"]
    F2["*.queue.jsonl"]
    F3["receipts.jsonl"]
  end

  F1 --> A2
  A2 --> Lib
  Lib --> A3
  A3 --> F2
  A3 --> F3
  A1 --> Lib
  A4 --> A3
```

## Target data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["ADRS projected fixed JSONL"] --> B["projected reader adapter"]
  B --> C["hq core+port lib"]
  C --> D["suggestion with compileDraft"]
  D --> E["acceptance"]
  E --> F["instruction"]
  F --> G["queue writer adapter"]
  G --> H["append-only queue JSONL row"]
```

## Phase 1: extract core+port as lib

### PR 1: Define hq core+port library boundary

Scope:

- Add or adjust docs explaining `core`, `port`, and `adapter` ownership.
- Add a package responsibility map.
- Add import/boundary guard if cheap.
- State that `source_ref` is opaque to core.

Done when:

- README or docs define `core+port as lib`.
- Adapter is named as the only concrete-schema owner.
- Core is documented as schema-independent.
- No behavior change.
- CI remains green.

### PR 2: Extract hq suggestion and acceptance semantics into core library

Scope:

- Move current context/suggestion/acceptance/instruction logic into a core package.
- Keep current behavior unchanged.
- Add core-level tests for existing behavior.
- Keep compileDraft semantics inside core.

Done when:

- Core can produce suggestions without knowing file schema.
- Core can finalize accepted suggestion into internal instruction.
- Core tests cover current fixture behavior.
- No queue row schema is introduced here.
- Existing CLI/proof tests still pass.

### PR 3: Route current CLI and file behavior through adapters

Scope:

- Introduce current adapter for existing proof/demo file shapes.
- Make CLI/REPL call core through port/adapters.
- Keep Linux/Windows proof behavior green.
- Preserve existing command behavior.

Done when:

- CLI uses adapter -> core -> adapter path.
- Existing proof files still work.
- Existing Linux/Windows Tab proof remains green.
- No external schema leaks into core.
- No product behavior expansion.

## Phase gate

Do not start Phase 2 until PR 1-3 are merged.

| Gate | Required |
|---|---:|
| core package exists | yes |
| port boundary exists | yes |
| current adapter exists | yes |
| CLI uses adapter path | yes |
| core has no ADRS projected dependency | yes |
| core has no queue JSONL dependency | yes |
| proof behavior still green | yes |

## Phase 2: add projected/queue schema adapters

### PR 4: Add hq queue envelope fixtures without runtime adapter

Scope:

- Add spec fixtures for queue row envelope.
- Define `id`, `target`, `op`, `source_ref`, `payload`, `status`, `provenance`, `created_at`.
- Define opaque `source_ref` examples.
- Define target examples: `ui.overlay`, `work.dispatch`, `adrs.proposal`, `receipt.close`.

Done when:

- Queue row fixture schema exists.
- `source_ref` is opaque.
- Target-specific payload is outside core authority.
- Invalid envelope fixtures fail.
- This PR does not write queue files at runtime.

### PR 5: Add ADRS projected reader adapter behind hq port

Scope:

- Read `ADRS projected fixed JSONL` into `JsonlWorld`.
- Map projected records to canonical core input.
- Preserve source identity as opaque `source_ref`.
- Add adapter fixtures.

Done when:

- Adapter consumes projected JSONL, not ADRS raw source.
- Adapter produces canonical core input.
- Core does not import adapter schema.
- `source_ref` survives mapping.
- Bad projected rows fail at adapter boundary.

### PR 6: Add append-only queue JSONL writer adapter

Scope:

- Convert accepted internal instruction to queue row.
- Append to file queue.
- Include `source_ref`, target, op, payload, provenance.
- Prove unaccepted suggestions do not write.

Done when:

- Accepted suggestion writes exactly one queue row.
- Unaccepted suggestion writes nothing.
- Queue append is deterministic.
- Queue row matches fixture envelope.
- Core does not serialize JSONL directly.
- Adapter owns queue JSONL formatting.

### PR 7: Add target-specific queue payload adapters

Targets:

| Target | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui.overlay` | Display overlay / selection / annotation |
| `work.dispatch` | Work item for ctx/ops/governance |
| `adrs.proposal` | Proposal candidate, not accepted authority |
| `receipt.close` | Close / reject / supersede queue item |

Done when:

- Target payload adapters are outside core.
- Unknown target is rejected or preserved only by explicit passthrough policy.
- `adrs.proposal` does not mutate ADRS authority.
- `ui.overlay` does not treat UI as state store.
- `work.dispatch` does not execute anything.

### PR 8: Prove fixed projected plus queue produces effective projection input

Scope:

- Add integration fixture: fixed projected + queue rows -> effective projection input.
- Prove queue overlay does not mutate fixed source.
- Prove proposal rows remain pending until accepted elsewhere.
- Add manifest/receipt fixture.

Done when:

- Fixed projected input remains unchanged.
- Queue rows create effective projection output.
- Effective projection is generated artifact, not authority.
- Proposal queue rows do not become ADRS accepted records.
- Receipts capture admitted/rejected/superseded rows.

## Explicit non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add ADRS raw parser | ADRS raw authority belongs in ADRS repo |
| Add remote API / DB | File-only phase |
| Add agent execution | hq builds queue; execution is outside |
| Add UI state store | UI reads projections and emits drafts only |
| Add schema adapter before lib extraction | Would leak external schema into core |
| Change product behavior during refactor | Phase 1 is boundary-only |

## Parent acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR 1-3 merged before any new projected/queue adapter PR is merged.
- [ ] `hq` has a clear `core+port as lib` boundary.
- [ ] Existing CLI/REPL/proof behavior goes through adapters.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse ADRS projected schema.

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Separate `hq` into a schema-independent `core+port as lib` and schema-dependent adapters before adding ADRS projected / queue schema adapters.

The intended sequence is strict:

1. First, extract and prove the `core+port as lib` boundary.
2. Then, add adapters for the proposed projected/queue schema.

This prevents ADRS projected schema, queue envelope schema, or target payload schema from leaking into hq core.

Refs #13.

## Final one-line shape

`hq core+port` is a reusable JSONL autocomplete compiler library.

Adapters translate concrete file schemas into and out of that library.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose | Directness |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Separate current behavior from concrete file/schema shapes | Direct |
| 1 | Make `core+port as lib` reusable and schema-independent | Direct |
| 2 | Keep ADRS raw/projected and queue envelope schemas outside core | Direct |
| 3 | Add projected/queue adapters only after the lib boundary is proved | Direct |
| 4 | Preserve file-only operation and append-only queue behavior | Direct |
| 5 | Make UI, hq, ADRS, and future targets reusable through adapters | Direct |
| 6 | Keep the implementation small and easy to sell/maintain | Indirect |
| 7 | Support high-margin software asset creation | Indirect |
| 8 | Support company value and sale-readiness | Meta |

## Non-negotiable dependency rule

| Layer | May depend on concrete schemas? | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| core | No | Owns meaning only |
| port | No | Owns abstract boundaries only |
| adapter | Yes | Owns file/schema translation |
| CLI/REPL runtime | Yes, through adapters | Must not parse concrete schemas inside core |
| tests/fixtures | Yes | Used to prove adapters and protocol behavior |

## Desired dependency direction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Lib["core+port as lib"]
    Core["core: context / suggestion / acceptance / instruction"]
    Port["port: read world / append instruction / clock / id / diagnostics"]
    Core --> Port
  end

  subgraph Adapters["schema adapters"]
    A1["current proof adapter"]
    A2["ADRS projected reader adapter"]
    A3["queue JSONL writer adapter"]
    A4["target payload adapters"]
  end

  subgraph Files["files"]
    F1["adrs.projected.fixed.jsonl"]
    F2["*.queue.jsonl"]
    F3["receipts.jsonl"]
  end

  F1 --> A2
  A2 --> Lib
  Lib --> A3
  A3 --> F2
  A3 --> F3
  A1 --> Lib
  A4 --> A3
```

## Target data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["ADRS projected fixed JSONL"] --> B["projected reader adapter"]
  B --> C["hq core+port lib"]
  C --> D["suggestion with compileDraft"]
  D --> E["acceptance"]
  E --> F["instruction"]
  F --> G["queue writer adapter"]
  G --> H["append-only queue JSONL row"]
```

## Phase 1: extract core+port as lib

### PR 1: Define hq core+port library boundary

Scope:

- Add or adjust docs explaining `core`, `port`, and `adapter` ownership.
- Add a package responsibility map.
- Add import/boundary guard if cheap.
- State that `source_ref` is opaque to core.

Done when:

- README or docs define `core+port as lib`.
- Adapter is named as the only concrete-schema owner.
- Core is documented as schema-independent.
- No behavior change.
- CI remains green.

### PR 2: Extract hq suggestion and acceptance semantics into core library

Scope:

- Move current context/suggestion/acceptance/instruction logic into a core package.
- Keep current behavior unchanged.
- Add core-level tests for existing behavior.
- Keep compileDraft semantics inside core.

Done when:

- Core can produce suggestions without knowing file schema.
- Core can finalize accepted suggestion into internal instruction.
- Core tests cover current fixture behavior.
- No queue row schema is introduced here.
- Existing CLI/proof tests still pass.

### PR 3: Route current CLI and file behavior through adapters

Scope:

- Introduce current adapter for existing proof/demo file shapes.
- Make CLI/REPL call core through port/adapters.
- Keep Linux/Windows proof behavior green.
- Preserve existing command behavior.

Done when:

- CLI uses adapter -> core -> adapter path.
- Existing proof files still work.
- Existing Linux/Windows Tab proof remains green.
- No external schema leaks into core.
- No product behavior expansion.

## Phase gate

Do not start Phase 2 until PR 1-3 are merged.

| Gate | Required |
|---|---:|
| core package exists | yes |
| port boundary exists | yes |
| current adapter exists | yes |
| CLI uses adapter path | yes |
| core has no ADRS projected dependency | yes |
| core has no queue JSONL dependency | yes |
| proof behavior still green | yes |

## Phase 2: add projected/queue schema adapters

### PR 4: Add hq queue envelope fixtures without runtime adapter

Scope:

- Add spec fixtures for queue row envelope.
- Define `id`, `target`, `op`, `source_ref`, `payload`, `status`, `provenance`, `created_at`.
- Define opaque `source_ref` examples.
- Define target examples: `ui.overlay`, `work.dispatch`, `adrs.proposal`, `receipt.close`.

Done when:

- Queue row fixture schema exists.
- `source_ref` is opaque.
- Target-specific payload is outside core authority.
- Invalid envelope fixtures fail.
- This PR does not write queue files at runtime.

### PR 5: Add ADRS projected reader adapter behind hq port

Scope:

- Read `ADRS projected fixed JSONL` into `JsonlWorld`.
- Map projected records to canonical core input.
- Preserve source identity as opaque `source_ref`.
- Add adapter fixtures.

Done when:

- Adapter consumes projected JSONL, not ADRS raw source.
- Adapter produces canonical core input.
- Core does not import adapter schema.
- `source_ref` survives mapping.
- Bad projected rows fail at adapter boundary.

### PR 6: Add append-only queue JSONL writer adapter

Scope:

- Convert accepted internal instruction to queue row.
- Append to file queue.
- Include `source_ref`, target, op, payload, provenance.
- Prove unaccepted suggestions do not write.

Done when:

- Accepted suggestion writes exactly one queue row.
- Unaccepted suggestion writes nothing.
- Queue append is deterministic.
- Queue row matches fixture envelope.
- Core does not serialize JSONL directly.
- Adapter owns queue JSONL formatting.

### PR 7: Add target-specific queue payload adapters

Targets:

| Target | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui.overlay` | Display overlay / selection / annotation |
| `work.dispatch` | Work item for ctx/ops/governance |
| `adrs.proposal` | Proposal candidate, not accepted authority |
| `receipt.close` | Close / reject / supersede queue item |

Done when:

- Target payload adapters are outside core.
- Unknown target is rejected or preserved only by explicit passthrough policy.
- `adrs.proposal` does not mutate ADRS authority.
- `ui.overlay` does not treat UI as state store.
- `work.dispatch` does not execute anything.

### PR 8: Prove fixed projected plus queue produces effective projection input

Scope:

- Add integration fixture: fixed projected + queue rows -> effective projection input.
- Prove queue overlay does not mutate fixed source.
- Prove proposal rows remain pending until accepted elsewhere.
- Add manifest/receipt fixture.

Done when:

- Fixed projected input remains unchanged.
- Queue rows create effective projection output.
- Effective projection is generated artifact, not authority.
- Proposal queue rows do not become ADRS accepted records.
- Receipts capture admitted/rejected/superseded rows.

## Explicit non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add ADRS raw parser | ADRS raw authority belongs in ADRS repo |
| Add remote API / DB | File-only phase |
| Add agent execution | hq builds queue; execution is outside |
| Add UI state store | UI reads projections and emits drafts only |
| Add schema adapter before lib extraction | Would leak external schema into core |
| Change product behavior during refactor | Phase 1 is boundary-only |

## Parent acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR 1-3 merged before any new projected/queue adapter PR is merged.
- [ ] `hq` has a clear `core+port as lib` boundary.
- [ ] Existing CLI/REPL/proof behavior goes through adapters.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse ADRS projected schema.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse hq queue JSONL envelope schema.
- [ ] Core treats `source_ref` as opaque.
- [ ] Existing proof-era behavior remains green.
- [ ] Adapter tests prove current behavior did not regress.
- [ ] ADRS raw schema remains outside hq.
- [ ] Queue adapter writes append-only JSONL rows.
- [ ] Unaccepted suggestions do not write queue rows.
- [ ] A reviewer can identify which files are core, port, adapter, fixtures, proof, and CLI.

## Destructive objections and defenses

| # | Objection | Defense |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Schema adapter leaks into core | Phase 1 must merge before adapter PRs |
| 2 | hq becomes ADRS-specific | Core treats `source_ref` as opaque |
| 3 | Queue row becomes ADRS raw shape | Queue envelope is independent |
| 4 | UI becomes state store | UI emits drafts; adapters write queue files |
| 5 | Fixed projection is mutated | Effective projection is generated output |
| 6 | Proposal and accepted authority mix | `adrs.proposal` remains pending queue target |
| 7 | Proof-era behavior breaks | PR3 preserves current proof through adapters |
| 8 | Adapter becomes huge | Split target payload adapters |
| 9 | Unknown target executes implicitly | Unknown target rejected or explicit passthrough only |
| 10 | Phase 2 starts too early | Parent issue requires Phase 1 gate |

## Final expected readback

`hq core+port as lib` is schema-independent and does not interpret ADRS or queue file shapes. Adapters translate ADRS projected input, queue output, and target payloads at the edge. The runtime remains file-only and append-only, and ADRS raw authority stays outside hq."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Separate `hq` into a schema-independent `core+port as lib` and schema-dependent adapters before adding ADRS projected / queue schema adapters.

The intended sequence is strict:

1. First, extract and prove the `core+port as lib` boundary.
2. Then, add adapters for the proposed projected/queue schema.

This prevents ADRS projected schema, queue envelope schema, or target payload schema from leaking into hq core.

Refs #13.

## Final one-line shape

`hq core+port` is a reusable JSONL autocomplete compiler library.

Adapters translate concrete file schemas into and out of that library.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose | Directness |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Separate current behavior from concrete file/schema shapes | Direct |
| 1 | Make `core+port as lib` reusable and schema-independent | Direct |
| 2 | Keep ADRS raw/projected and queue envelope schemas outside core | Direct |
| 3 | Add projected/queue adapters only after the lib boundary is proved | Direct |
| 4 | Preserve file-only operation and append-only queue behavior | Direct |
| 5 | Make UI, hq, ADRS, and future targets reusable through adapters | Direct |
| 6 | Keep the implementation small and easy to sell/maintain | Indirect |
| 7 | Support high-margin software asset creation | Indirect |
| 8 | Support company value and sale-readiness | Meta |

## Non-negotiable dependency rule

| Layer | May depend on concrete schemas? | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| core | No | Owns meaning only |
| port | No | Owns abstract boundaries only |
| adapter | Yes | Owns file/schema translation |
| CLI/REPL runtime | Yes, through adapters | Must not parse concrete schemas inside core |
| tests/fixtures | Yes | Used to prove adapters and protocol behavior |

## Desired dependency direction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Lib["core+port as lib"]
    Core["core: context / suggestion / acceptance / instruction"]
    Port["port: read world / append instruction / clock / id / diagnostics"]
    Core --> Port
  end

  subgraph Adapters["schema adapters"]
    A1["current proof adapter"]
    A2["ADRS projected reader adapter"]
    A3["queue JSONL writer adapter"]
    A4["target payload adapters"]
  end

  subgraph Files["files"]
    F1["adrs.projected.fixed.jsonl"]
    F2["*.queue.jsonl"]
    F3["receipts.jsonl"]
  end

  F1 --> A2
  A2 --> Lib
  Lib --> A3
  A3 --> F2
  A3 --> F3
  A1 --> Lib
  A4 --> A3
```

## Target data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["ADRS projected fixed JSONL"] --> B["projected reader adapter"]
  B --> C["hq core+port lib"]
  C --> D["suggestion with compileDraft"]
  D --> E["acceptance"]
  E --> F["instruction"]
  F --> G["queue writer adapter"]
  G --> H["append-only queue JSONL row"]
```

## Phase 1: extract core+port as lib

### PR 1: Define hq core+port library boundary

Scope:

- Add or adjust docs explaining `core`, `port`, and `adapter` ownership.
- Add a package responsibility map.
- Add import/boundary guard if cheap.
- State that `source_ref` is opaque to core.

Done when:

- README or docs define `core+port as lib`.
- Adapter is named as the only concrete-schema owner.
- Core is documented as schema-independent.
- No behavior change.
- CI remains green.

### PR 2: Extract hq suggestion and acceptance semantics into core library

Scope:

- Move current context/suggestion/acceptance/instruction logic into a core package.
- Keep current behavior unchanged.
- Add core-level tests for existing behavior.
- Keep compileDraft semantics inside core.

Done when:

- Core can produce suggestions without knowing file schema.
- Core can finalize accepted suggestion into internal instruction.
- Core tests cover current fixture behavior.
- No queue row schema is introduced here.
- Existing CLI/proof tests still pass.

### PR 3: Route current CLI and file behavior through adapters

Scope:

- Introduce current adapter for existing proof/demo file shapes.
- Make CLI/REPL call core through port/adapters.
- Keep Linux/Windows proof behavior green.
- Preserve existing command behavior.

Done when:

- CLI uses adapter -> core -> adapter path.
- Existing proof files still work.
- Existing Linux/Windows Tab proof remains green.
- No external schema leaks into core.
- No product behavior expansion.

## Phase gate

Do not start Phase 2 until PR 1-3 are merged.

| Gate | Required |
|---|---:|
| core package exists | yes |
| port boundary exists | yes |
| current adapter exists | yes |
| CLI uses adapter path | yes |
| core has no ADRS projected dependency | yes |
| core has no queue JSONL dependency | yes |
| proof behavior still green | yes |

## Phase 2: add projected/queue schema adapters

### PR 4: Add hq queue envelope fixtures without runtime adapter

Scope:

- Add spec fixtures for queue row envelope.
- Define `id`, `target`, `op`, `source_ref`, `payload`, `status`, `provenance`, `created_at`.
- Define opaque `source_ref` examples.
- Define target examples: `ui.overlay`, `work.dispatch`, `adrs.proposal`, `receipt.close`.

Done when:

- Queue row fixture schema exists.
- `source_ref` is opaque.
- Target-specific payload is outside core authority.
- Invalid envelope fixtures fail.
- This PR does not write queue files at runtime.

### PR 5: Add ADRS projected reader adapter behind hq port

Scope:

- Read `ADRS projected fixed JSONL` into `JsonlWorld`.
- Map projected records to canonical core input.
- Preserve source identity as opaque `source_ref`.
- Add adapter fixtures.

Done when:

- Adapter consumes projected JSONL, not ADRS raw source.
- Adapter produces canonical core input.
- Core does not import adapter schema.
- `source_ref` survives mapping.
- Bad projected rows fail at adapter boundary.

### PR 6: Add append-only queue JSONL writer adapter

Scope:

- Convert accepted internal instruction to queue row.
- Append to file queue.
- Include `source_ref`, target, op, payload, provenance.
- Prove unaccepted suggestions do not write.

Done when:

- Accepted suggestion writes exactly one queue row.
- Unaccepted suggestion writes nothing.
- Queue append is deterministic.
- Queue row matches fixture envelope.
- Core does not serialize JSONL directly.
- Adapter owns queue JSONL formatting.

### PR 7: Add target-specific queue payload adapters

Targets:

| Target | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui.overlay` | Display overlay / selection / annotation |
| `work.dispatch` | Work item for ctx/ops/governance |
| `adrs.proposal` | Proposal candidate, not accepted authority |
| `receipt.close` | Close / reject / supersede queue item |

Done when:

- Target payload adapters are outside core.
- Unknown target is rejected or preserved only by explicit passthrough policy.
- `adrs.proposal` does not mutate ADRS authority.
- `ui.overlay` does not treat UI as state store.
- `work.dispatch` does not execute anything.

### PR 8: Prove fixed projected plus queue produces effective projection input

Scope:

- Add integration fixture: fixed projected + queue rows -> effective projection input.
- Prove queue overlay does not mutate fixed source.
- Prove proposal rows remain pending until accepted elsewhere.
- Add manifest/receipt fixture.

Done when:

- Fixed projected input remains unchanged.
- Queue rows create effective projection output.
- Effective projection is generated artifact, not authority.
- Proposal queue rows do not become ADRS accepted records.
- Receipts capture admitted/rejected/superseded rows.

## Explicit non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add ADRS raw parser | ADRS raw authority belongs in ADRS repo |
| Add remote API / DB | File-only phase |
| Add agent execution | hq builds queue; execution is outside |
| Add UI state store | UI reads projections and emits drafts only |
| Add schema adapter before lib extraction | Would leak external schema into core |
| Change product behavior during refactor | Phase 1 is boundary-only |

## Parent acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR 1-3 merged before any new projected/queue adapter PR is merged.
- [ ] `hq` has a clear `core+port as lib` boundary.
- [ ] Existing CLI/REPL/proof behavior goes through adapters.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse ADRS projected schema.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse hq queue JSONL envelope schema.
- [ ] Core treats `source_ref` as opaque.
- [ ] Existing proof-era behavior remains green.
- [ ] Adapter tests prove current behavior did not regress.
- [ ] ADRS raw schema remains outside hq.
- [ ] Queue adapter writes append-only JSONL rows.
- [ ] Unaccepted suggestions do not write queue rows.
- [ ] A reviewer can identify which files are core, port, adapter, fixtures, proof, and CLI.

## Destructive objections and defenses

| # | Objection | Defense |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Schema adapter leaks into core | Phase 1 must merge before adapter PRs |
| 2 | hq becomes ADRS-specific | Core treats `source_ref` as opaque |
| 3 | Queue row becomes ADRS raw shape | Queue envelope is independent |
| 4 | UI becomes state store | UI emits drafts; adapters write queue files |
| 5 | Fixed projection is mutated | Effective projection is generated output |
| 6 | Proposal and accepted authority mix | `adrs.proposal` remains pending queue target |
| 7 | Proof-era behavior breaks | PR3 preserves current proof through adapters |
| 8 | Adapter becomes huge | Split target payload adapters |
| 9 | Unknown target executes implicitly | Unknown target rejected or explicit passthrough only |
| 10 | Phase 2 starts too early | Parent issue requires Phase 1 gate |

## Final expected readback

`hq core+port as lib` is schema-independent and does not interpret ADRS or queue file shapes. Adapters translate ADRS projected input, queue output, and target payloads at the edge. The runtime remains file-only and append-only, and ADRS raw authority stays outside hq."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Separate `hq` into a schema-independent `core+port as lib` and schema-dependent adapters before adding ADRS projected / queue schema adapters.

The intended sequence is strict:

1. First, extract and prove the `core+port as lib` boundary.
2. Then, add adapters for the proposed projected/queue schema.

This prevents ADRS projected schema, queue envelope schema, or target payload schema from leaking into hq core.

Refs #13.

## Final one-line shape

`hq core+port` is a reusable JSONL autocomplete compiler library.

Adapters translate concrete file schemas into and out of that library.

## Purpose lineage

| Generation | Purpose | Directness |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | Separate current behavior from concrete file/schema shapes | Direct |
| 1 | Make `core+port as lib` reusable and schema-independent | Direct |
| 2 | Keep ADRS raw/projected and queue envelope schemas outside core | Direct |
| 3 | Add projected/queue adapters only after the lib boundary is proved | Direct |
| 4 | Preserve file-only operation and append-only queue behavior | Direct |
| 5 | Make UI, hq, ADRS, and future targets reusable through adapters | Direct |
| 6 | Keep the implementation small and easy to sell/maintain | Indirect |
| 7 | Support high-margin software asset creation | Indirect |
| 8 | Support company value and sale-readiness | Meta |

## Non-negotiable dependency rule

| Layer | May depend on concrete schemas? | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| core | No | Owns meaning only |
| port | No | Owns abstract boundaries only |
| adapter | Yes | Owns file/schema translation |
| CLI/REPL runtime | Yes, through adapters | Must not parse concrete schemas inside core |
| tests/fixtures | Yes | Used to prove adapters and protocol behavior |

## Desired dependency direction

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph Lib["core+port as lib"]
    Core["core: context / suggestion / acceptance / instruction"]
    Port["port: read world / append instruction / clock / id / diagnostics"]
    Core --> Port
  end

  subgraph Adapters["schema adapters"]
    A1["current proof adapter"]
    A2["ADRS projected reader adapter"]
    A3["queue JSONL writer adapter"]
    A4["target payload adapters"]
  end

  subgraph Files["files"]
    F1["adrs.projected.fixed.jsonl"]
    F2["*.queue.jsonl"]
    F3["receipts.jsonl"]
  end

  F1 --> A2
  A2 --> Lib
  Lib --> A3
  A3 --> F2
  A3 --> F3
  A1 --> Lib
  A4 --> A3
```

## Target data flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A["ADRS projected fixed JSONL"] --> B["projected reader adapter"]
  B --> C["hq core+port lib"]
  C --> D["suggestion with compileDraft"]
  D --> E["acceptance"]
  E --> F["instruction"]
  F --> G["queue writer adapter"]
  G --> H["append-only queue JSONL row"]
```

## Phase 1: extract core+port as lib

### PR 1: Define hq core+port library boundary

Scope:

- Add or adjust docs explaining `core`, `port`, and `adapter` ownership.
- Add a package responsibility map.
- Add import/boundary guard if cheap.
- State that `source_ref` is opaque to core.

Done when:

- README or docs define `core+port as lib`.
- Adapter is named as the only concrete-schema owner.
- Core is documented as schema-independent.
- No behavior change.
- CI remains green.

### PR 2: Extract hq suggestion and acceptance semantics into core library

Scope:

- Move current context/suggestion/acceptance/instruction logic into a core package.
- Keep current behavior unchanged.
- Add core-level tests for existing behavior.
- Keep compileDraft semantics inside core.

Done when:

- Core can produce suggestions without knowing file schema.
- Core can finalize accepted suggestion into internal instruction.
- Core tests cover current fixture behavior.
- No queue row schema is introduced here.
- Existing CLI/proof tests still pass.

### PR 3: Route current CLI and file behavior through adapters

Scope:

- Introduce current adapter for existing proof/demo file shapes.
- Make CLI/REPL call core through port/adapters.
- Keep Linux/Windows proof behavior green.
- Preserve existing command behavior.

Done when:

- CLI uses adapter -> core -> adapter path.
- Existing proof files still work.
- Existing Linux/Windows Tab proof remains green.
- No external schema leaks into core.
- No product behavior expansion.

## Phase gate

Do not start Phase 2 until PR 1-3 are merged.

| Gate | Required |
|---|---:|
| core package exists | yes |
| port boundary exists | yes |
| current adapter exists | yes |
| CLI uses adapter path | yes |
| core has no ADRS projected dependency | yes |
| core has no queue JSONL dependency | yes |
| proof behavior still green | yes |

## Phase 2: add projected/queue schema adapters

### PR 4: Add hq queue envelope fixtures without runtime adapter

Scope:

- Add spec fixtures for queue row envelope.
- Define `id`, `target`, `op`, `source_ref`, `payload`, `status`, `provenance`, `created_at`.
- Define opaque `source_ref` examples.
- Define target examples: `ui.overlay`, `work.dispatch`, `adrs.proposal`, `receipt.close`.

Done when:

- Queue row fixture schema exists.
- `source_ref` is opaque.
- Target-specific payload is outside core authority.
- Invalid envelope fixtures fail.
- This PR does not write queue files at runtime.

### PR 5: Add ADRS projected reader adapter behind hq port

Scope:

- Read `ADRS projected fixed JSONL` into `JsonlWorld`.
- Map projected records to canonical core input.
- Preserve source identity as opaque `source_ref`.
- Add adapter fixtures.

Done when:

- Adapter consumes projected JSONL, not ADRS raw source.
- Adapter produces canonical core input.
- Core does not import adapter schema.
- `source_ref` survives mapping.
- Bad projected rows fail at adapter boundary.

### PR 6: Add append-only queue JSONL writer adapter

Scope:

- Convert accepted internal instruction to queue row.
- Append to file queue.
- Include `source_ref`, target, op, payload, provenance.
- Prove unaccepted suggestions do not write.

Done when:

- Accepted suggestion writes exactly one queue row.
- Unaccepted suggestion writes nothing.
- Queue append is deterministic.
- Queue row matches fixture envelope.
- Core does not serialize JSONL directly.
- Adapter owns queue JSONL formatting.

### PR 7: Add target-specific queue payload adapters

Targets:

| Target | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ui.overlay` | Display overlay / selection / annotation |
| `work.dispatch` | Work item for ctx/ops/governance |
| `adrs.proposal` | Proposal candidate, not accepted authority |
| `receipt.close` | Close / reject / supersede queue item |

Done when:

- Target payload adapters are outside core.
- Unknown target is rejected or preserved only by explicit passthrough policy.
- `adrs.proposal` does not mutate ADRS authority.
- `ui.overlay` does not treat UI as state store.
- `work.dispatch` does not execute anything.

### PR 8: Prove fixed projected plus queue produces effective projection input

Scope:

- Add integration fixture: fixed projected + queue rows -> effective projection input.
- Prove queue overlay does not mutate fixed source.
- Prove proposal rows remain pending until accepted elsewhere.
- Add manifest/receipt fixture.

Done when:

- Fixed projected input remains unchanged.
- Queue rows create effective projection output.
- Effective projection is generated artifact, not authority.
- Proposal queue rows do not become ADRS accepted records.
- Receipts capture admitted/rejected/superseded rows.

## Explicit non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add ADRS raw parser | ADRS raw authority belongs in ADRS repo |
| Add remote API / DB | File-only phase |
| Add agent execution | hq builds queue; execution is outside |
| Add UI state store | UI reads projections and emits drafts only |
| Add schema adapter before lib extraction | Would leak external schema into core |
| Change product behavior during refactor | Phase 1 is boundary-only |

## Parent acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR 1-3 merged before any new projected/queue adapter PR is merged.
- [ ] `hq` has a clear `core+port as lib` boundary.
- [ ] Existing CLI/REPL/proof behavior goes through adapters.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse ADRS projected schema.
- [ ] Core does not import or parse hq queue JSONL envelope schema.
- [ ] Core treats `source_ref` as opaque.
- [ ] Existing proof-era behavior remains green.
- [ ] Adapter tests prove current behavior did not regress.
- [ ] ADRS raw schema remains outside hq.
- [ ] Queue adapter writes append-only JSONL rows.
- [ ] Unaccepted suggestions do not write queue rows.
- [ ] A reviewer can identify which files are core, port, adapter, fixtures, proof, and CLI.

## Destructive objections and defenses

| # | Objection | Defense |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Schema adapter leaks into core | Phase 1 must merge before adapter PRs |
| 2 | hq becomes ADRS-specific | Core treats `source_ref` as opaque |
| 3 | Queue row becomes ADRS raw shape | Queue envelope is independent |
| 4 | UI becomes state store | UI emits drafts; adapters write queue files |
| 5 | Fixed projection is mutated | Effective projection is generated output |
| 6 | Proposal and accepted authority mix | `adrs.proposal` remains pending queue target |
| 7 | Proof-era behavior breaks | PR3 preserves current proof through adapters |
| 8 | Adapter becomes huge | Split target payload adapters |
| 9 | Unknown target executes implicitly | Unknown target rejected or explicit passthrough only |
| 10 | Phase 2 starts too early | Parent issue requires Phase 1 gate |

## Final expected readback

`hq core+port as lib` is schema-independent and does not interpret ADRS or queue file shapes. Adapters translate ADRS projected input, queue output, and target payloads at the edge. The runtime remains file-only and append-only, and ADRS raw authority stays outside hq."}

request.text:
{"body":"## 背景

`adrs#439` のUI担当整理には今も有効な不変条件がある一方、現行 `ui` と `adrs#468` の議論から、一般化しすぎた部分が明確になった。

本Issueは #439 を置換しない。UI repo側で、**残す不変条件と訂正する設計を分離し、今後の実装Issue/PRの前提を一意にする**。

Refs:
- roccho-dev/adrs#439
- roccho-dev/adrs#468
- #207
- #212
- #277
- #310
- #311

## 反証

| #439 の記述 | 反証・訂正 |
|---|---|
| **物理構成を大きく整理する案**（19→13 package、components改名、core-port解体、別app入口統合等） | **完成条件にはしない。** #310で、必要性未証明の物理再編は外し、既存ownerで満たせるなら移動・新package不要と再評価済み。 |
| **shellとopsはUI Library consumerとして同格** | **library利用という局所では成立するが、E2E topologyとして一般化しすぎ。** `adrs#468` では UI が安全な Projection / View / URL / HTML を完成させ、OPS はその成果物を delivery / readback する下流consumerになり得る。OPSが常にprojection/coreまで直接consumeする必要はない。 |
| **U05: 必要情報を満たす同じ意味データをgraph / seq / mapへ渡す** | **“同じ意味データ”を同一bytes・同一shapeと読むのは強すぎる。** 守るべきは、同じsemantic sourceから意味を複製せず、view固有のprojection/adaptationを決定的に作れること。rendererごとの業務モデル複製は禁止するが、renderer-neutral projectionとrenderer固有adapterは許容する。 |
| **graph / seq / map を複数viewの中心として扱う** | **軸が不足する。** 同じDev向け完全データから、`ops × execute → checklist`、`client × agree → agreement sheet`、`team × understand → architecture graph` のような投影が必要。したがって `audience / purpose / view` は独立軸として扱う。 |
| **UIにも意味・状態・処理がある** | **範囲限定が必要。** UIがownしてよいのはUI-domain、projection、interaction、presentation state。upstreamの業務意味、開示可否、正式permission、effect/admission authorityをUIへ吸収しない。 |
| A2UI / Semantic Mapの関係 | **上下関係をarchitecture invariantにしない。** Semantic MapがA2UI内componentとしてcomposeされるのは有力だが、常に `Sem in A2UI`、または両者が完全に同じpayload shapeを読むことまでは要求しない。必要な意味が同じsource/projectionから導かれることだけを固定する。 |

## 残す不変条件

- 表示方式ごとにbusiness meaningを複製しない。
- renderer / SVG / maxGraph / generated HTMLをmeaning authorityにしない。
- semantic meaning と layout / camera / presentation stateを分離する。
- 同じUI能力をconsumerごとに再実装しない。
- UI内部のselection / history / edit ownerを重複させない。
- provider/runtime/effect authorityをUIへ取り込まない。

## 更新後の最小正規形

```text
Upstream Source
  ↓
Project(
  audience_ref,   # required dimension, values are open
  purpose_ref     # independent from audience
)
  ↓
Allowed Projection
  ↓
View(
  view_ref,
  focus,
  depth / LOD
)
  ↓
Renderer / Adapter
  ├─ A2UI
  └─ Semantic Map / other existing capability
  ↓
artifact-invocation / Host
  ↓
URL / portable HTML
```

意味は次の通り。

```text
Audience = 誰にどの世界を渡してよいか
Purpose  = その人が何をするためか
View     = その仕事をどう見るか
Renderer = そのViewをどう描くか
Host     = そのViewをどう再現・実行するか
```

`audience` は次元として必須だが、`dev / client / ops / team` をenumにはしない。値集合はopenで、exact trusted profileとして追加・削除できる。unknown / stale profileをroot/devへ暗黙fallbackしない。

同様に、`checklist / agreement-sheet / graph / seq / map` をaudienceへ直結しない。たとえばclientがgraphを見ることも、opsがgraphで調査することも許容する。

## 結論

**#439の核心は「one semantic source → multiple reusable UI projections」で維持する。**

ただし次は後継設計として修正する。

- 物理package再編を完成条件にしない。
- shell = ops同格をE2E全体へ一般化しない。
- same data = 同一bytes / 同一shape としない。
- graph / seq / mapだけをview体系としない。
- A2UI / Semantic Mapの固定上下関係を要求しない。

実装は新frameworkではなく、既存ownerへ最小差分として閉じる。

```text
ADRS = cross-repo完成形
repo Issue = そのrepoの完成形
PR = exact implementation + test + proof
```

## 本Issueの役割

このIssueはUI側の設計訂正・正規化だけを所有する。

- 実装完成状態: #311
- Semantic Map/editor owner: #207
- UI library responsibility: #212
- same source → graph/seq/map: #277
- repo再整理記録: #310
- cross-repo completion: roccho-dev/adrs#468

本Issue自体は実装完了、merge、deploy、外部配信の許可を意味しない。"}

{"body":"## 背景

`adrs#439` のUI担当整理には今も有効な不変条件がある一方、現行 `ui` と `adrs#468` の議論から、一般化しすぎた部分が明確になった。

本Issueは #439 を置換しない。UI repo側で、**残す不変条件と訂正する設計を分離し、今後の実装Issue/PRの前提を一意にする**。

Refs:
- roccho-dev/adrs#439
- roccho-dev/adrs#468
- #207
- #212
- #277
- #310
- #311

## 反証

| #439 の記述 | 反証・訂正 |
|---|---|
| **物理構成を大きく整理する案**（19→13 package、components改名、core-port解体、別app入口統合等） | **完成条件にはしない。** #310で、必要性未証明の物理再編は外し、既存ownerで満たせるなら移動・新package不要と再評価済み。 |
| **shellとopsはUI Library consumerとして同格** | **library利用という局所では成立するが、E2E topologyとして一般化しすぎ。** `adrs#468` では UI が安全な Projection / View / URL / HTML を完成させ、OPS はその成果物を delivery / readback する下流consumerになり得る。OPSが常にprojection/coreまで直接consumeする必要はない。 |
| **U05: 必要情報を満たす同じ意味データをgraph / seq / mapへ渡す** | **“同じ意味データ”を同一bytes・同一shapeと読むのは強すぎる。** 守るべきは、同じsemantic sourceから意味を複製せず、view固有のprojection/adaptationを決定的に作れること。rendererごとの業務モデル複製は禁止するが、renderer-neutral projectionとrenderer固有adapterは許容する。 |
| **graph / seq / map を複数viewの中心として扱う** | **軸が不足する。** 同じDev向け完全データから、`ops × execute → checklist`、`client × agree → agreement sheet`、`team × understand → architecture graph` のような投影が必要。したがって `audience / purpose / view` は独立軸として扱う。 |
| **UIにも意味・状態・処理がある** | **範囲限定が必要。** UIがownしてよいのはUI-domain、projection、interaction、presentation state。upstreamの業務意味、開示可否、正式permission、effect/admission authorityをUIへ吸収しない。 |
| A2UI / Semantic Mapの関係 | **上下関係をarchitecture invariantにしない。** Semantic MapがA2UI内componentとしてcomposeされるのは有力だが、常に `Sem in A2UI`、または両者が完全に同じpayload shapeを読むことまでは要求しない。必要な意味が同じsource/projectionから導かれることだけを固定する。 |

## 残す不変条件

- 表示方式ごとにbusiness meaningを複製しない。
- renderer / SVG / maxGraph / generated HTMLをmeaning authorityにしない。
- semantic meaning と layout / camera / presentation stateを分離する。
- 同じUI能力をconsumerごとに再実装しない。
- UI内部のselection / history / edit ownerを重複させない。
- provider/runtime/effect authorityをUIへ取り込まない。

## 更新後の最小正規形

```text
Upstream Source
  ↓
Project(
  audience_ref,   # required dimension, values are open
  purpose_ref     # independent from audience
)
  ↓
Allowed Projection
  ↓
View(
  view_ref,
  focus,
  depth / LOD
)
  ↓
Renderer / Adapter
  ├─ A2UI
  └─ Semantic Map / other existing capability
  ↓
artifact-invocation / Host
  ↓
URL / portable HTML
```

意味は次の通り。

```text
Audience = 誰にどの世界を渡してよいか
Purpose  = その人が何をするためか
View     = その仕事をどう見るか
Renderer = そのViewをどう描くか
Host     = そのViewをどう再現・実行するか
```

`audience` は次元として必須だが、`dev / client / ops / team` をenumにはしない。値集合はopenで、exact trusted profileとして追加・削除できる。unknown / stale profileをroot/devへ暗黙fallbackしない。

同様に、`checklist / agreement-sheet / graph / seq / map` をaudienceへ直結しない。たとえばclientがgraphを見ることも、opsがgraphで調査することも許容する。

## 結論

**#439の核心は「one semantic source → multiple reusable UI projections」で維持する。**

ただし次は後継設計として修正する。

- 物理package再編を完成条件にしない。
- shell = ops同格をE2E全体へ一般化しない。
- same data = 同一bytes / 同一shape としない。
- graph / seq / mapだけをview体系としない。
- A2UI / Semantic Mapの固定上下関係を要求しない。

実装は新frameworkではなく、既存ownerへ最小差分として閉じる。

```text
ADRS = cross-repo完成形
repo Issue = そのrepoの完成形
PR = exact implementation + test + proof
```

## 本Issueの役割

このIssueはUI側の設計訂正・正規化だけを所有する。

- 実装完成状態: #311
- Semantic Map/editor owner: #207
- UI library responsibility: #212
- same source → graph/seq/map: #277
- repo再整理記録: #310
- cross-repo completion: roccho-dev/adrs#468

本Issue自体は実装完了、merge、deploy、外部配信の許可を意味しない。"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

After #13, the repo identity and authority boundaries are much cleaner: `hq` is documented as protocol-first, Go-runtime, Python-tooling, and evidence-bounded.

The remaining gap is runtime authority: the Windows/Linux-proven value still appears to live in the reflective runtime surface, while the official product command must be `cmd/hq`.

This issue promotes the implemented reflective runtime value into the official `hq` command so the repo is not only well-organized but also product-runtime coherent.

## Problem

Current risk:

| Area | Risk |
|---|---|
| official command | `README` / repo identity point at `hq`, but the proven interactive runtime may still be under reflective naming |
| scripts / CI | Some checks may still treat `cmd/hq-reflective` or `hq-reflective-*` artifacts as the practical runtime |
| Windows proof | Windows functionality exists, but must prove the official `hq` binary, not a proof-only command |
| UX claim | Screenshots/proofs show parts of the desired UX, but official `hq` must own complete input -> suggestion -> accept -> instruction behavior |
| buyer/maintainer readback | A reviewer should not need to know historical proof names to find the product runtime |

## Final one-line shape

`cmd/hq` is the official terminal runtime for JSONL-aware autocomplete compilation.

It supports context-aware completion, compileDraft preview, accepted suggestion finalization, and append-only instruction JSONL output on Linux and Windows.

## Scope

Promote the working reflective runtime into official `hq` identity.

Required scope:

- make `cmd/hq` the real runtime entrypoint
- ensure `cmd/hq` supports the proven runtime flags and behavior
- update scripts and CI to build/test the official `hq` binary
- run Linux and Windows interactive Tab proof against `hq`, not a proof-only binary
- keep or remove `cmd/hq-reflective` only as a documented compatibility wrapper, not product authority
- align README, docs, screenshots/proof references, and artifacts with official `hq`

## Required product behavior

| Behavior | Required result |
|---|---|
| `hq --complete` | returns schema/cursor-aware suggestions |
| `hq --context` | returns structured cursor context |
| `hq --draft` | returns compileDraft / instruction preview |
| `hq --queue` | appends only accepted/finalized instruction rows |
| interactive Tab | shows visible candidates from schema context |
| Ctrl-T / preview path | exposes candidate compileDraft where supported |
| Enter / accept path | accepted suggestion can become instruction JSONL |
| no accept | no queue write |
| Linux / Windows | both prove literal Tab input against official `hq` binary |

## Acceptance criteria

This issue can close only when all are true:

- [ ] `cmd/hq/main.go` is a real runtime entrypoint, not an empty placeholder.
- [ ] Official build path is `go build ./cmd/hq` or documented equivalent.
- [ ] Built binary names use `hq-*`, not `hq-reflective-*`, for official proof artifacts.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` builds/tests `cmd/hq` as the product runtime.
- [ ] Linux interactive Tab proof runs against the official `hq` binary.
- [ ] Windows interactive Tab proof runs against the official `hq` binary.
- [ ] Proof artifacts still include `SENT_KEYS`, `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209`, and visible proof schema candidates.
- [ ] `--complete`, `--context`, and `--draft` smoke paths work through `cmd/hq`.
- [ ] If `cmd/hq-reflective` remains, it is a compatibility wrapper or historical proof adapter, not a second official runtime.
- [ ] README examples and docs use the official `hq` command path and binary names.
- [ ] Protocol fixture tests still pass.
- [ ] CI / Windows reflective proof / Interactive Tab proof all pass on the final PR head.

## Non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add remote API execution | `hq` creates/queues instructions; execution belongs elsewhere |
| Add agent behavior | Keep this issue focused on official runtime promotion |
| Expand business schemas | First make runtime identity coherent |
| Replace Linux/Windows interactive proof with `--complete` only | Would weaken the Tab UX proof |
| Reopen old POC PRs | Old proof material is evidence/history, not product authority |

## Suggested PR slicing

Prefer one small PR if feasible. If it grows, split as:

| PR | Scope |
|---:|---|
| 1 | `cmd/hq` real entrypoint + scripts/check.sh update |
| 2 | Linux/Windows proof workflows retargeted to official `hq` binary |
| 3 | README/docs/artifact naming cleanup |

## Final expected readback

A reviewer should be able to say:

> The official product runtime is `cmd/hq`. The same command owns JSONL-aware completion, context, draft, queue append, and Linux/Windows interactive Tab proof. Any reflective/proof naming is historical or compatibility-only, not product authority.

If that sentence is not true after the PRs, this issue is not complete."}
