{"body":"## Purpose

After #13, the repo identity and authority boundaries are much cleaner: `hq` is documented as protocol-first, Go-runtime, Python-tooling, and evidence-bounded.

The remaining gap is runtime authority: the Windows/Linux-proven value still appears to live in the reflective runtime surface, while the official product command must be `cmd/hq`.

This issue promotes the implemented reflective runtime value into the official `hq` command so the repo is not only well-organized but also product-runtime coherent.

## Problem

Current risk:

| Area | Risk |
|---|---|
| official command | `README` / repo identity point at `hq`, but the proven interactive runtime may still be under reflective naming |
| scripts / CI | Some checks may still treat `cmd/hq-reflective` or `hq-reflective-*` artifacts as the practical runtime |
| Windows proof | Windows functionality exists, but must prove the official `hq` binary, not a proof-only command |
| UX claim | Screenshots/proofs show parts of the desired UX, but official `hq` must own complete input -> suggestion -> accept -> instruction behavior |
| buyer/maintainer readback | A reviewer should not need to know historical proof names to find the product runtime |

## Final one-line shape

`cmd/hq` is the official terminal runtime for JSONL-aware autocomplete compilation.

It supports context-aware completion, compileDraft preview, accepted suggestion finalization, and append-only instruction JSONL output on Linux and Windows.

## Scope

Promote the working reflective runtime into official `hq` identity.

Required scope:

- make `cmd/hq` the real runtime entrypoint
- ensure `cmd/hq` supports the proven runtime flags and behavior
- update scripts and CI to build/test the official `hq` binary
- run Linux and Windows interactive Tab proof against `hq`, not a proof-only binary
- keep or remove `cmd/hq-reflective` only as a documented compatibility wrapper, not product authority
- align README, docs, screenshots/proof references, and artifacts with official `hq`

## Required product behavior

| Behavior | Required result |
|---|---|
| `hq --complete` | returns schema/cursor-aware suggestions |
| `hq --context` | returns structured cursor context |
| `hq --draft` | returns compileDraft / instruction preview |
| `hq --queue` | appends only accepted/finalized instruction rows |
| interactive Tab | shows visible candidates from schema context |
| Ctrl-T / preview path | exposes candidate compileDraft where supported |
| Enter / accept path | accepted suggestion can become instruction JSONL |
| no accept | no queue write |
| Linux / Windows | both prove literal Tab input against official `hq` binary |

## Acceptance criteria

This issue can close only when all are true:

- [ ] `cmd/hq/main.go` is a real runtime entrypoint, not an empty placeholder.
- [ ] Official build path is `go build ./cmd/hq` or documented equivalent.
- [ ] Built binary names use `hq-*`, not `hq-reflective-*`, for official proof artifacts.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` builds/tests `cmd/hq` as the product runtime.
- [ ] Linux interactive Tab proof runs against the official `hq` binary.
- [ ] Windows interactive Tab proof runs against the official `hq` binary.
- [ ] Proof artifacts still include `SENT_KEYS`, `SENT_BYTES_HEX: 7b2209`, and visible proof schema candidates.
- [ ] `--complete`, `--context`, and `--draft` smoke paths work through `cmd/hq`.
- [ ] If `cmd/hq-reflective` remains, it is a compatibility wrapper or historical proof adapter, not a second official runtime.
- [ ] README examples and docs use the official `hq` command path and binary names.
- [ ] Protocol fixture tests still pass.
- [ ] CI / Windows reflective proof / Interactive Tab proof all pass on the final PR head.

## Non-goals

| Non-goal | Reason |
|---|---|
| Add remote API execution | `hq` creates/queues instructions; execution belongs elsewhere |
| Add agent behavior | Keep this issue focused on official runtime promotion |
| Expand business schemas | First make runtime identity coherent |
| Replace Linux/Windows interactive proof with `--complete` only | Would weaken the Tab UX proof |
| Reopen old POC PRs | Old proof material is evidence/history, not product authority |

## Suggested PR slicing

Prefer one small PR if feasible. If it grows, split as:

| PR | Scope |
|---:|---|
| 1 | `cmd/hq` real entrypoint + scripts/check.sh update |
| 2 | Linux/Windows proof workflows retargeted to official `hq` binary |
| 3 | README/docs/artifact naming cleanup |

## Final expected readback

A reviewer should be able to say:

> The official product runtime is `cmd/hq`. The same command owns JSONL-aware completion, context, draft, queue append, and Linux/Windows interactive Tab proof. Any reflective/proof naming is historical or compatibility-only, not product authority.

If that sentence is not true after the PRs, this issue is not complete."}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose
Define the exact editor-to-compiler boundary so Vim sends cursor/buffer/schema/queue data only, never adapter-specific execution meaning.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Keeps `vim -> hq` as compile/accept only. |
| product | Preserves editor portability. |
| system/org | Prevents Vim from knowing Herdr/Codex/Claude/sh details. |
| business/meta | Supports small replaceable editor surfaces. |

## Scope
- Define buffer, cursor, schema path, queue path, accept payload, and error handling.
- Document that worker/adapters are downstream.

## Non-scope
- Worker execution.
- Vim UI polish.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Contract doc exists.
- [ ] Vim side has no target adapter responsibility.
- [ ] `hq --complete`, `--draft`, and `--accept --queue` map to the contract.

## Breaking cases
- [ ] Vim plugin launches Herdr/Codex/Claude directly as part of acceptance path.
- [ ] Vim completion output diverges from hq CLI output.

## Evidence
- Contract doc.
- Example command flows.

## Merge condition
Merge only when Vim is only an editor surface over `hq`, not an execution surface."}

criteria.no: 本文は期待・役割・入出力の設計・条件・仮定・架空の受入例だけで、実際の観測を報告していない。

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Refactor `packages/auto-complete` so the reusable core is a small library with ports, while JSONL/HQ sources become source adapters.

Why this contributes to the higher purpose: it keeps the LSP completion asset reusable across Vim, Helix, and hq without binding core logic to one data format or one editor. This protects the CI-proven behavior while making the package easier to extend and review.

## Current issue

The current code has the right behavior, but the conceptual boundary can still be cleaner.

`jp-jsonl`, `domain-jsonl`, and `hq-source-jsonl` should not live in core/provider implementation space. They are concrete source adapters that satisfy core ports.

## Target boundary

```text
core port as lib
+
source adapters
+
transport adapters
+
editor adapters
+
app wiring
```

## Target tree shape

```text
packages/auto-complete/
├── lib/
│   └── jpcmp/
│       ├── core/
│       │   ├── candidate.go
│       │   ├── completion.go
│       │   ├── rank.go
│       │   ├── replace_range.go
│       │   ├── romaji.go
│       │   ├── token.go
│       │   └── types.go
│       └── ports/
│           ├── provider.go
│           ├── projection.go
│           ├── request.go
│           └── response.go
├── app/
│   └── jpcmp-lsp/
│       ├── wire.go
│       ├── registry.go
│       └── config.go
├── adapters/
│   ├── source/
│   │   ├── jp-jsonl/
│   │   ├── domain-jsonl/
│   │   └── hq-source-jsonl/
│   ├── transport/
│   │   └── lsp/
│   └── editor/
│       ├── vim/
│       └── helix/
├── data/
├── proofs/
├── docs/
└── test/
```

## Refactor rules

- No behavior change to candidate-contract output.
- No behavior change to Go LSP JSON-RPC output.
- No behavior change to Vim -> Go LSP adapter proof.
- No behavior change to UX visual artifact content.
- `core` must not import JSONL source adapters, LSP server code, Vim, or Helix.
- source adapters may import core ports and return normalized candidates.
- LSP adapter maps core responses to LSP only.
- app wiring owns concrete adapter registry.

## No-degrade CI gate

All existing checks must keep passing:

- current Vim candidate-contract proof
- golden summary invariants
- Go tests
- Go LSP JSON-RPC smoke
- Vim adapter through Go LSP
- UX visual evidence render/check/upload
- adapter boundary check
- Helix config smoke check

## Done when

- PR references this issue.
- `lib/jpcmp/core` and `lib/jpcmp/ports` exist.
- concrete JSONL/HQ sources live under `adapters/source/*`.
- concrete LSP transport lives under `adapters/transport/lsp`.
- concrete Vim/Helix editor assets live under `adapters/editor/*`.
- `cmd/jpcmp-lsp` or `app/jpcmp-lsp` wires concrete adapters without placing adapter logic in core.
- boundary check is updated to enforce the new layout.
- all existing CI gates pass.
"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Refactor `packages/auto-complete` so the reusable core is a small library with ports, while JSONL/HQ sources become source adapters.

Why this contributes to the higher purpose: it keeps the LSP completion asset reusable across Vim, Helix, and hq without binding core logic to one data format or one editor. This protects the CI-proven behavior while making the package easier to extend and review.

## Current issue

The current code has the right behavior, but the conceptual boundary can still be cleaner.

`jp-jsonl`, `domain-jsonl`, and `hq-source-jsonl` should not live in core/provider implementation space. They are concrete source adapters that satisfy core ports.

## Target boundary

```text
core port as lib
+
source adapters
+
transport adapters
+
editor adapters
+
app wiring
```

## Target tree shape

```text
packages/auto-complete/
├── lib/
│   └── jpcmp/
│       ├── core/
│       │   ├── candidate.go
│       │   ├── completion.go
│       │   ├── rank.go
│       │   ├── replace_range.go
│       │   ├── romaji.go
│       │   ├── token.go
│       │   └── types.go
│       └── ports/
│           ├── provider.go
│           ├── projection.go
│           ├── request.go
│           └── response.go
├── app/
│   └── jpcmp-lsp/
│       ├── wire.go
│       ├── registry.go
│       └── config.go
├── adapters/
│   ├── source/
│   │   ├── jp-jsonl/
│   │   ├── domain-jsonl/
│   │   └── hq-source-jsonl/
│   ├── transport/
│   │   └── lsp/
│   └── editor/
│       ├── vim/
│       └── helix/
├── data/
├── proofs/
├── docs/
└── test/
```

## Refactor rules

- No behavior change to candidate-contract output.
- No behavior change to Go LSP JSON-RPC output.
- No behavior change to Vim -> Go LSP adapter proof.
- No behavior change to UX visual artifact content.
- `core` must not import JSONL source adapters, LSP server code, Vim, or Helix.
- source adapters may import core ports and return normalized candidates.
- LSP adapter maps core responses to LSP only.
- app wiring owns concrete adapter registry.

## No-degrade CI gate

All existing checks must keep passing:

- current Vim candidate-contract proof
- golden summary invariants
- Go tests
- Go LSP JSON-RPC smoke
- Vim adapter through Go LSP
- UX visual evidence render/check/upload
- adapter boundary check
- Helix config smoke check

## Done when

- PR references this issue.
- `lib/jpcmp/core` and `lib/jpcmp/ports` exist.
- concrete JSONL/HQ sources live under `adapters/source/*`.
- concrete LSP transport lives under `adapters/transport/lsp`.
- concrete Vim/Helix editor assets live under `adapters/editor/*`.
- `cmd/jpcmp-lsp` or `app/jpcmp-lsp` wires concrete adapters without placing adapter logic in core.
- boundary check is updated to enforce the new layout.
- all existing CI gates pass.
"}

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Remove the repository-specific DVM boundary and prevent it from being replaced by `RenderAst`, `RenderingIR`, or another independent current-state schema.

The current repository correctly keeps `events.jsonl` as the only authority, but it then creates multiple derived state models before producing draw.io/SVG/D2 artifacts. This increases translation code, parity gates and edit-writeback risk without adding authority.

## Decision

```text
events.jsonl = authority and append history
reducer local maps = private transient implementation only
mxGraphModel = sole generated current state
projections/editors = consumers of mxGraphModel
```

All semantic metadata must live in draw.io XML user objects that wrap `mxCell`. Geometry, style, source/target, parentage and bendpoints remain native `mxCell`/`mxGeometry` state.

This issue supersedes only the DVM/SemanticIR/RenderingIR ownership clauses of #2, #4 and #5. It preserves their useful contracts: `events.jsonl` authority, validation before append, semantic/visual separation, stable IDs, replaceable projections and proof receipts.

## Why now

The attached executable proof shows:

- direct `events.jsonl -> mxGraphModel` reduction;
- 15 event operations and eight editor command forms;
- 13 diagram kinds projected to native draw.io, SVG, image-exact draw.io, D2, Graphviz, text and geometry metrics;
- semantic/visual hash isolation;
- invalid edits rejected before append;
- no DVM, RenderAst, RenderingIR, custom `*IR`, public snapshot API or independent state artifact;
- Venn membership and ERD columns preserved in XML user objects;
- semantic recovery still works after editor-style normalization removes nonstandard attributes from nested `mxCell`.

The current canonical Venn artifact is valid draw.io XML but does not contain its source `meta.members`. The proof candidate retains all seven Venn membership records in `metaJson` on XML user objects.

## Required changes

- Replace reducer DVM output with direct `mxGraphModel` output.
- Remove DVM validation, public CLI output and `dvm.json` fixtures.
- Remove RenderAst/RenderingIR and adapter inputs based on them.
- Retarget D2, SVG, draw.io, Graphviz/ELK, text, proof and quality code to `mxGraphModel`.
- Retarget roundtrip hashes and diffs to semantic and visual selections from `mxGraphModel`.
- Keep event schemas and reject-before-append behavior.
- Add a repo-wide no-custom-IR gate.

## Acceptance gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 Authority | `events.jsonl` remains the only authority |
| G2 Direct reduction | events reduce directly to `mxGraphModel` |
| G3 Metadata completeness | every canonical event field survives in XML user objects/cells |
| G4 Exact fixture parity | all 13 canonical event logs preserve accepted semantic counts, IDs, order and metadata |
| G5 Output parity | SVG, native draw.io, image-exact draw.io, D2 and locked layout outputs pass |
| G6 Roundtrip | semantic and visual commands append one valid event and re-reduce |
| G7 Isolation | visual edits do not change semantic hash; semantic-only edits do not change visual hash |
| G8 Negative behavior | invalid events/commands fail before append |
| G9 Editor persistence | pinned draw.io open/load/getXml/save preserves user objects, IDs and graph links |
| G10 No duplicate IR | repo-wide DVM/RenderAst/RenderingIR/custom-IR/artifact count is zero |
| G11 Determinism | two clean builds are byte-equivalent except explicitly allowed fields |
| G12 UI evidence | exact geometry/edge metrics are emitted with unresolved warnings, not false green |
| G13 Nix | `nix flake check` and package build pass |
| G14 Exact-head CI | every required job is green on the PR head |
| G15 Rollback | previous accepted artifacts remain available until cutover proof is accepted |

## Destructive cases

The proof package contains 15 destructive cases. It must fail closed for metadata loss, duplicate state reintroduction, ambiguous IDs, invalid append, semantic/visual hash contamination, editor metadata stripping, canonical fixture drift, locked-engine drift and unsupported UI exactness claims.

## Delivery split

### PR A — proof and contract

- add the executable no-DVM proof;
- add current-baseline audit and destructive cases;
- record this decision and exact cutover gates;
- add a proof CI job;
- do not delete canonical DVM yet.

### PR B — canonical cutover

- replace the canonical pipeline;
- delete all DVM/RenderAst/RenderingIR surfaces;
- pass G1–G15 on the exact head;
- merge only after proof artifact review.

## Current evidence status

```text
current canonical baseline audit   PASS
replacement mechanism proof        PASS
proposal readiness                  PASS
exact canonical cutover             NOT_RUN
```

The issue can be accepted now. It closes only after PR B passes G1–G15 and the repo-wide duplicate-IR count is zero."}

The current repository correctly keeps `events.jsonl` as the only authority, but it then creates multiple derived state models before producing draw.io/SVG/D2 artifacts. This increases translation code, parity gates and edit-writeback risk without adding authority.

## Decision

```text
events.jsonl = authority and append history
reducer local maps = private transient implementation only
mxGraphModel = sole generated current state
projections/editors = consumers of mxGraphModel
```

All semantic metadata must live in draw.io XML user objects that wrap `mxCell`. Geometry, style, source/target, parentage and bendpoints remain native `mxCell`/`mxGeometry` state.

This issue supersedes only the DVM/SemanticIR/RenderingIR ownership clauses of #2, #4 and #5. It preserves their useful contracts: `events.jsonl` authority, validation before append, semantic/visual separation, stable IDs, replaceable projections and proof receipts.

## Why now

The attached executable proof shows:

- direct `events.jsonl -> mxGraphModel` reduction;
- 15 event operations and eight editor command forms;
- 13 diagram kinds projected to native draw.io, SVG, image-exact draw.io, D2, Graphviz, text and geometry metrics;
- semantic/visual hash isolation;
- invalid edits rejected before append;
- no DVM, RenderAst, RenderingIR, custom `*IR`, public snapshot API or independent state artifact;
- Venn membership and ERD columns preserved in XML user objects;
- semantic recovery still works after editor-style normalization removes nonstandard attributes from nested `mxCell`.

The current canonical Venn artifact is valid draw.io XML but does not contain its source `meta.members`. The proof candidate retains all seven Venn membership records in `metaJson` on XML user objects.

## Required changes

- Replace reducer DVM output with direct `mxGraphModel` output.
- Remove DVM validation, public CLI output and `dvm.json` fixtures.
- Remove RenderAst/RenderingIR and adapter inputs based on them.
- Retarget D2, SVG, draw.io, Graphviz/ELK, text, proof and quality code to `mxGraphModel`.
- Retarget roundtrip hashes and diffs to semantic and visual selections from `mxGraphModel`.
- Keep event schemas and reject-before-append behavior.
- Add a repo-wide no-custom-IR gate.

## Acceptance gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 Authority | `events.jsonl` remains the only authority |
| G2 Direct reduction | events reduce directly to `mxGraphModel` |
| G3 Metadata completeness | every canonical event field survives in XML user objects/cells |
| G4 Exact fixture parity | all 13 canonical event logs preserve accepted semantic counts, IDs, order and metadata |
| G5 Output parity | SVG, native draw.io, image-exact draw.io, D2 and locked layout outputs pass |
| G6 Roundtrip | semantic and visual commands append one valid event and re-reduce |
| G7 Isolation | visual edits do not change semantic hash; semantic-only edits do not change visual hash |
| G8 Negative behavior | invalid events/commands fail before append |
| G9 Editor persistence | pinned draw.io open/load/getXml/save preserves user objects, IDs and graph links |
| G10 No duplicate IR | repo-wide DVM/RenderAst/RenderingIR/custom-IR/artifact count is zero |
| G11 Determinism | two clean builds are byte-equivalent except explicitly allowed fields |
| G12 UI evidence | exact geometry/edge metrics are emitted with unresolved warnings, not false green |
| G13 Nix | `nix flake check` and package build pass |
| G14 Exact-head CI | every required job is green on the PR head |
| G15 Rollback | previous accepted artifacts remain available until cutover proof is accepted |

## Destructive cases

The proof package contains 15 destructive cases. It must fail closed for metadata loss, duplicate state reintroduction, ambiguous IDs, invalid append, semantic/visual hash contamination, editor metadata stripping, canonical fixture drift, locked-engine drift and unsupported UI exactness claims.

## Delivery split

### PR A — proof and contract

- add the executable no-DVM proof;
- add current-baseline audit and destructive cases;
- record this decision and exact cutover gates;
- add a proof CI job;
- do not delete canonical DVM yet.

### PR B — canonical cutover

- replace the canonical pipeline;
- delete all DVM/RenderAst/RenderingIR surfaces;
- pass G1–G15 on the exact head;
- merge only after proof artifact review.

## Current evidence status

```text
current canonical baseline audit   PASS
replacement mechanism proof        PASS
proposal readiness                  PASS
exact canonical cutover             NOT_RUN
```

The issue can be accepted now. It closes only after PR B passes G1–G15 and the repo-wide duplicate-IR count is zero."}

request.text:
{"body":"<!-- phase2-typed-launcher-false-positive-exclusion-20261018 -->
## 目的

Windows→resources移行で、必要性を実証していない任意のtyped launcherを必須機能・必須依存へ昇格させた偽陽性を排除する。Userの「偽陽性なら排除issueたててスキップ、残未完了を完遂進めて」に基づく切り出しであり、今回の移行で新dual launcherの提供・実鍵呼出し・有償再測定を要求しない。

## 根拠と除外対象

- [訂正・独立再評価](https://github.com/roccho-org/envs/pull/104#pullrequestreview-5562557238)：Appsの任意PoC手順とOpsの下流互換説明を、通常build/dev/CIの必須依存として誤分類した。
- Apps `2c13d9196047bd420358ae0cebdd7eb2fc0d99cd` の[通常構成](https://github.com/roccho-dev/apps/blob/2c13d9196047bd420358ae0cebdd7eb2fc0d99cd/flake.nix#L88-L168)はOpsの完成済みJev/TypeLLM ESMをWorkerへ組み込む。[Windows typedLaunch手順](https://github.com/roccho-dev/apps/blob/2c13d9196047bd420358ae0cebdd7eb2fc0d99cd/README.md#L160-L193)は明示選択のsource-dev/PoC再実行用。
- Ops `b8e1e4849f30e1873fc2f6108323c27193d6e707` の[説明](https://github.com/roccho-org/ops/blob/b8e1e4849f30e1873fc2f6108323c27193d6e707/packages/typellm/README.md#L49-L74)は下流Windows wrapperがOps CLIを使う方向で、OpsのWindows必須入力ではない。
- 除外するのは「この任意dual launcherを新提供しなければフェーズ2未達」という追加要件。TypeLLMそのものや通常のOps提供まで不要と判定していない。検索0件だけを無依存の根拠にしない。

## 今回の処遇：移行からスキップ

- [x] 任意dual launcherの新規移植・新実鍵/有償再試験をフェーズ2の完成条件から外す。
- [x] [中央envs104](https://github.com/roccho-org/envs/pull/104)、[提供側resources37](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/pull/37)、[旧停止Windows102](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/pull/102)の必須FAIL判定を撤回。元の正常・異常・継続・復旧試験、PoC履歴・元手順は保持する。
- [x] このIssueを上記の現在本文へ関連付け、独立readbackで今回の除外と必要な残件の判定が一致することを確認した。[7PRの訂正・残件最終確認5562670378](https://github.com/roccho-org/envs/pull/104#pullrequestreview-5562670378)。

既存[PR46](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/pull/46)のsingle TypeLLM CLIは別の実在する機能・成果であり、旧dualとの同等性や実鍵成功を本Issueから推定しない。その既存機能や説明の追加削減は、本Issueに具体的な現役caller・owner・利用目的と削減影響を揃えて必要性を再評価する。単なる移行gateからの除外を理由に、別系列の機能を無断削除しない。本Issueはその要否の追跡先であり、移行完了を待たせる依存にはしない。

過去の個別safety/policy拒否は詳細原因UNKNOWNのまま保持する。今回の「必須判定の偽陽性」は、拒否自体の誤検知確定や同一/等価要求を別tool・actor・経路で再送する許可ではない。

## 移行の正本と出口

[対象定義resources25](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/25#issuecomment-6242263448)と[固定供給版・既知必要役割の独立受入](https://github.com/roccho-org/envs/pull/104#pullrequestreview-5562598896)へ帰着する。提供・依存移行・更新運用の通常FAILが実在すれば元の試験を維持してfix/checkする。任意機能・全最新feature採用・notes明確化・全Host/state調査を新gateにしない。Archive/削除・本番Host適用は今回行わない。

実行担当は既存Codex root、独立確認は既存pr31_completion。ADRS `a6284e58ed99243447e135828d983fc07d2d363e`・#449原則に従い、実装方法や順序をこのIssueで指定しない。"}

criteria.no: 本文に実現すべき状態の宣言がない。見出しの名前を除くと実施報告・観測・経緯だけである。

{"body":"## Purpose

Implement the governance-side org join that combines required repo universe, packet registry, packet findings, and producer verification into repo-level organization-active or blocking finding rows.

Parent phase issue: #80

## Scope

This is an issue for a future governance implementation PR. Do not open or implement the PR from this issue alone.

## Requirements

- Consume D1 required repo universe output.
- Consume D2 packet registry/transport output.
- Consume D3 packet finding output.
- Consume Phase C producer provenance verifier output where available.
- Join required repo rows with packet rows and producer verification rows.
- Produce `organization-active` only when required repo packet exists, validates, is fresh, and producer provenance checks pass.
- Produce blocking finding when a required repo is missing a packet.
- Produce blocking finding when packet is stale, malformed, unavailable, or unpinned.
- Produce blocking finding when producer provenance is invalid.
- Produce blocking finding when packet source cannot be associated with the required repo row.
- Emit deterministic `govOrgPackageOutput` or accepted equivalent org join output.
- Include expected/actual/delta/likelyOwner/nextAction and relevant digests in each blocking finding.
- Keep org join as evidence/admission precursor only, not branch protection authority by itself.

## Done when

- Clean governance/adrs fixture produces organization-active rows.
- Missing packet fixture produces blocking finding and nonzero strict-mode check.
- Stale packet fixture produces blocking finding.
- Invalid provenance fixture produces blocking finding.
- Unrequired packet fixture is diagnosed as orphan or ignored according to accepted contract.
- Output can be consumed later by final-scope join without reinterpreting semantics.

## Not done when

- Packet existence alone produces organization-active.
- Missing/stale/invalid packet is warning-only.
- Producer provenance is ignored.
- Org join hardcodes required repo universe outside ADRS input.
- PR claims final gate, branch protection, downstream rollout, or all-package final admission.

## Evidence required in child PR

- Org join tool/check path.
- Input fixture paths for required repo universe, packet registry, packet findings, producer verification.
- Clean org join output.
- Dirty fixture outputs for missing packet, stale packet, invalid provenance.
- Strict-mode nonzero check evidence.

## Child PR comment template

```text
Child PR: governance#<number>
Phase issue: #80 / D4
Requirement: provenance-aware org join
Delta removed: required repo can no longer become active from packet existence alone
Evidence: <org join path / fixtures / strict check output>
Boundary: org join only; no final gate/branch protection/downstream rollout claim
```
"}

旧構成案は履歴として保持する。**下の旧案は現行の完成目標・実移管指示ではない。** 既存[resources roccho-dev/windows#10](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/10)・[windows roccho-dev/resources#52](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/52)・[windows roccho-dev/resources#60](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/60)の実装と未完条件は維持。実際のsource/配備/秘密/認証/CI/ArchiveをこのIssue更新だけで変更・許可・完了しない。

<details>
<summary>旧案：OS/OCI/flakeをresourcesへ集約するツリー（2026-10-10時点の履歴）</summary>

## 目的

NixOS・Windows・非NixOSのNix OCIと、そのOS/user設定・IaCをresourcesに集約する。現windowsの責務を保ち、正本を重複させない。

基準: [windows proposals / 615ea7d](https://github.com/roccho-dev/windows/tree/615ea7d97edaf5889bd7968f5a1feb90b8297b09)の全46ファイル。

## 完成形案

```text
resources/
├─ flake.nix / flake.lock       # 合成・公開output・依存固定
├─ profile/                    # 共通dev profile・gh・release pin・fonts
├─ nixos/                      # 新設: OS/user設定とhost入力
├─ windows/                    # 現hosts/common: 宣言→pack→native適用
├─ oci/
│  ├─ common.nix               # own/rentの共有実装だけ
│  ├─ dev/                     # 公式Nix bootstrap＋trusted dev image
│  ├─ own/                     # local開発・専用home/work/nix
│  └─ rent/                    # remote開発・SSH/Tunnel・状態継続
├─ extensions/
│  ├─ github/                  # 既存の限定root
│  ├─ git-state/               # backendとsynthetic proof
│  ├─ release-watch/           # release検証・更新提案
│  └─ cloudflare/              # 将来: envsからIaCを移管
├─ docs/                       # 設計・受入・移行記録
└─ .github/workflows/          # 既存の検証・配布を保持
```

## 条件

- dev/own/rentは用途・信頼境界。専用profileまで無理に一つにしない。
- manifestは宣言から生成する。Windows用の第二のBindingを手編集しない。
- envsは暗号化秘密・供給/配置・受渡し記録を担当。provider rootの移管は別工程とし、同じ資源の正本を二つ作らない。
- 既存proof、固定source、状態継続・復旧の境界を残す。image名・volume名・ledger・state backendはrepo移動に合わせて一括改名しない。

まずREADME案をPRで提示する。このIssue/PRは構成提案であり、IaC移行・provider/state操作・windows退役は含めない。


</details>

{"body":"## Status and authority

```text
record: UI_INVOCATION_INDEX_RED_001
status: CANON_TDD_RED_SPEC_OPEN__IMPLEMENTATION_NOT_STARTED
parent: roccho-dev/ui#190
decision: roccho-dev/adrs#347
upstream: roccho-dev/ui#191
downstream: roccho-dev/ops#327
sequence: 3/7

opening_authorizes_merge: false
opening_authorizes_provider_effect: false
index_authority: false
accepted_meaning_authority: false
```

This Issue defines one independently mergeable index projection after the exact invocation identity/reference exists. It creates no PR and may be rebased onto the exact current UI head.

## Expected effect

Exact UI Release manifests and invocation/browser receipts become one deterministic, searchable JSONL index that is rendered by the same Artifact Shell. No hand-maintained link page, per-decision HTML, database, search server, or second application is needed.

```text
exact Release manifests
+ exact invocation receipts
→ deterministic artifact-invocation-index.jsonl
→ one version-fixed catalog invocation
→ existing Artifact Shell
```

The index can be deleted and rebuilt byte-identically from its exact inputs. It is a non-authority projection, not a publication or decision ledger.

## Completed behavior

1. Accept only exact Release manifests, exact invocation/browser receipts, and explicit title/source metadata projections.
2. Generate `artifact-invocation-index.jsonl` with stable row identity, canonical field order, and stable sort independent of filesystem enumeration order.
3. Each current-format row binds at least invocation ID/reference, semantic ID/title, state/profile/kernel digests, capability ID/version, invocation schema, projection intent, Release/source refs, and latest observation ref.
4. New-format rows use Release-root-relative invocation references, not provider-bound absolute URLs.
5. Identical duplicate records deduplicate deterministically.
6. Conflicting duplicates with the same identity fail closed.
7. Missing, failed, or incomplete observations remain visible; they are not silently dropped.
8. `exact`, `state-pinned`, `unknown`, and `broken` are derived from fixed facts and observations rather than stored as mutable publication truth.
9. Reordering inputs does not change output bytes or digest.
10. Two clean builds from the same exact input set produce byte-identical index bytes and digest.
11. Adding one valid invocation adds one row without changing unrelated rows.
12. Removing an input Release removes only its derived row on rebuild; no hidden retained state exists.
13. The index is opened through the existing Artifact Shell using an existing capability, preferably `render.a2ui@1`, or `render.semantic-map@1` only when its existing contract is a natural fit.
14. Direct navigation, refresh, search/filter, and opening an indexed invocation preserve exact references.
15. The rendered page visibly marks index authority as false and exposes source/receipt traceability.
16. No new runtime, route application, persistent store, database, server-side search, or second index schema family is added.

## Kent Beck Canon TDD RED contract

Before production implementation, add the smallest pure-reducer and real-browser RED suite. Each test must fail for a named absent behavior while existing repository checks remain Green.

Required Canon REDs:

1. `same_exact_input_set_builds_byte_identically`.
2. `filesystem_input_order_does_not_change_index`.
3. `stable_row_identity_is_derived_from_exact_invocation`.
4. `identical_duplicate_is_deduped`.
5. `conflicting_duplicate_fails_closed`.
6. `one_new_invocation_adds_only_one_row`.
7. `unrelated_row_bytes_remain_stable`.
8. `missing_or_failed_observation_is_not_dropped`.
9. `mutable_status_is_derived_not_stored_as_authority`.
10. `new_rows_keep_release_root_relative_invocation_ref`.
11. `provider_origin_is_absent_from_new_index_identity`.
12. `index_rebuild_requires_no_previous_index_file`.
13. `index_is_rendered_by_existing_artifact_shell`.
14. `direct_navigation_and_refresh_preserve_catalog_identity`.
15. `indexed_link_opens_exact_invocation`.
16. `index_displays_authority_false_and_exact_source_refs`.
17. `malformed_manifest_or_receipt_fails_closed`.
18. `unknown_schema_version_fails_closed`.
19. `no_dedicated_index_app_database_or_search_server_is_added`.
20. `repository_wide_checks_remain_green`.

The initial RED evidence must record exact baseline commit/tree, input fixture digests, test names, and one expected failure reason per test. A RED caused by a broken fixture, missing browser binary, import error, or already-Red baseline is invalid.

## Merge permission

Merge is permitted only when all are true:

- `ui#191` is merged or its exact immutable output contract is pinned;
- every Canon RED was first observed Red for the intended missing behavior and is now Green;
- two clean index builds are byte-identical;
- the index can be deleted and reconstructed only from exact manifests/receipts/metadata inputs;
- generated rows contain no provider secret, mutable credential URL, or authority claim;
- existing Artifact Shell, invocation, A2UI/Semantic Map, browser, and repository-wide checks remain Green;
- no required test was skipped, deleted, weakened, or changed to mirror the implementation;
- the exact PR head/tree, input-set digest, index bytes/digest, catalog invocation ID/reference, and browser receipt are recorded;
- no provider deploy, current update, public-selection, accepted-meaning, or production-cutover claim is made.

## Likely ownership surface

Prefer a thin pure reducer under the existing Artifact Shell publication owner and existing runtime tests. Create a new file only when no current script owns deterministic publication aggregation.

```text
apps/artifact-shell/scripts/**
apps/artifact-shell/src/publication.mjs
apps/artifact-shell/tests/**
existing render capability fixtures
```

Do not create `apps/invocation-index`, an index server, or a second catalog framework.

## Non-goals

```text
provider deployment or remote readback
legacy URL discovery/import
current/latest alias
new renderer/capability without a proven missing primitive
publication or decision authority
full-text server search
```

## Done

Close only when a fresh reviewer can remove the generated index, rebuild it twice from the exact Release evidence, obtain identical bytes, open it through the existing Artifact Shell, find and open exact invocation references, observe explicit failed/unknown rows rather than hidden omissions, and confirm the complete existing UI suite remains Green."}

```text
record: UI_INVOCATION_INDEX_RED_001
status: CANON_TDD_RED_SPEC_OPEN__IMPLEMENTATION_NOT_STARTED
parent: roccho-dev/ui#190
decision: roccho-dev/adrs#347
upstream: roccho-dev/ui#191
downstream: roccho-dev/ops#327
sequence: 3/7

opening_authorizes_merge: false
opening_authorizes_provider_effect: false
index_authority: false
accepted_meaning_authority: false
```

This Issue defines one independently mergeable index projection after the exact invocation identity/reference exists. It creates no PR and may be rebased onto the exact current UI head.

## Expected effect

Exact UI Release manifests and invocation/browser receipts become one deterministic, searchable JSONL index that is rendered by the same Artifact Shell. No hand-maintained link page, per-decision HTML, database, search server, or second application is needed.

```text
exact Release manifests
+ exact invocation receipts
→ deterministic artifact-invocation-index.jsonl
→ one version-fixed catalog invocation
→ existing Artifact Shell
```

The index can be deleted and rebuilt byte-identically from its exact inputs. It is a non-authority projection, not a publication or decision ledger.

## Completed behavior

1. Accept only exact Release manifests, exact invocation/browser receipts, and explicit title/source metadata projections.
2. Generate `artifact-invocation-index.jsonl` with stable row identity, canonical field order, and stable sort independent of filesystem enumeration order.
3. Each current-format row binds at least invocation ID/reference, semantic ID/title, state/profile/kernel digests, capability ID/version, invocation schema, projection intent, Release/source refs, and latest observation ref.
4. New-format rows use Release-root-relative invocation references, not provider-bound absolute URLs.
5. Identical duplicate records deduplicate deterministically.
6. Conflicting duplicates with the same identity fail closed.
7. Missing, failed, or incomplete observations remain visible; they are not silently dropped.
8. `exact`, `state-pinned`, `unknown`, and `broken` are derived from fixed facts and observations rather than stored as mutable publication truth.
9. Reordering inputs does not change output bytes or digest.
10. Two clean builds from the same exact input set produce byte-identical index bytes and digest.
11. Adding one valid invocation adds one row without changing unrelated rows.
12. Removing an input Release removes only its derived row on rebuild; no hidden retained state exists.
13. The index is opened through the existing Artifact Shell using an existing capability, preferably `render.a2ui@1`, or `render.semantic-map@1` only when its existing contract is a natural fit.
14. Direct navigation, refresh, search/filter, and opening an indexed invocation preserve exact references.
15. The rendered page visibly marks index authority as false and exposes source/receipt traceability.
16. No new runtime, route application, persistent store, database, server-side search, or second index schema family is added.

## Kent Beck Canon TDD RED contract

Before production implementation, add the smallest pure-reducer and real-browser RED suite. Each test must fail for a named absent behavior while existing repository checks remain Green.

Required Canon REDs:

1. `same_exact_input_set_builds_byte_identically`.
2. `filesystem_input_order_does_not_change_index`.
3. `stable_row_identity_is_derived_from_exact_invocation`.
4. `identical_duplicate_is_deduped`.
5. `conflicting_duplicate_fails_closed`.
6. `one_new_invocation_adds_only_one_row`.
7. `unrelated_row_bytes_remain_stable`.
8. `missing_or_failed_observation_is_not_dropped`.
9. `mutable_status_is_derived_not_stored_as_authority`.
10. `new_rows_keep_release_root_relative_invocation_ref`.
11. `provider_origin_is_absent_from_new_index_identity`.
12. `index_rebuild_requires_no_previous_index_file`.
13. `index_is_rendered_by_existing_artifact_shell`.
14. `direct_navigation_and_refresh_preserve_catalog_identity`.
15. `indexed_link_opens_exact_invocation`.
16. `index_displays_authority_false_and_exact_source_refs`.
17. `malformed_manifest_or_receipt_fails_closed`.
18. `unknown_schema_version_fails_closed`.
19. `no_dedicated_index_app_database_or_search_server_is_added`.
20. `repository_wide_checks_remain_green`.

The initial RED evidence must record exact baseline commit/tree, input fixture digests, test names, and one expected failure reason per test. A RED caused by a broken fixture, missing browser binary, import error, or already-Red baseline is invalid.

## Merge permission

Merge is permitted only when all are true:

- `ui#191` is merged or its exact immutable output contract is pinned;
- every Canon RED was first observed Red for the intended missing behavior and is now Green;
- two clean index builds are byte-identical;
- the index can be deleted and reconstructed only from exact manifests/receipts/metadata inputs;
- generated rows contain no provider secret, mutable credential URL, or authority claim;
- existing Artifact Shell, invocation, A2UI/Semantic Map, browser, and repository-wide checks remain Green;
- no required test was skipped, deleted, weakened, or changed to mirror the implementation;
- the exact PR head/tree, input-set digest, index bytes/digest, catalog invocation ID/reference, and browser receipt are recorded;
- no provider deploy, current update, public-selection, accepted-meaning, or production-cutover claim is made.

## Likely ownership surface

Prefer a thin pure reducer under the existing Artifact Shell publication owner and existing runtime tests. Create a new file only when no current script owns deterministic publication aggregation.

```text
apps/artifact-shell/scripts/**
apps/artifact-shell/src/publication.mjs
apps/artifact-shell/tests/**
existing render capability fixtures
```

Do not create `apps/invocation-index`, an index server, or a second catalog framework.

## Non-goals

```text
provider deployment or remote readback
legacy URL discovery/import
current/latest alias
new renderer/capability without a proven missing primitive
publication or decision authority
full-text server search
```

## Done

Close only when a fresh reviewer can remove the generated index, rebuild it twice from the exact Release evidence, obtain identical bytes, open it through the existing Artifact Shell, find and open exact invocation references, observe explicit failed/unknown rows rather than hidden omissions, and confirm the complete existing UI suite remains Green."}

17. `malformed_manifest_or_receipt_fails_closed`.
18. `unknown_schema_version_fails_closed`.

```
